e5335126adb0cf23: JOHOR BARU: Johor recorded 13,641 dengue cases and 18 deaths as of yesterday, marking a 159.4 per cent increase in infections and an 80 per cent rise in fatalities compared with the corresponding period last year.
State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said 275 cases were reported in Epidemiological Week 45, up 3.4 per cent from 266 cases the previous week.
Johor Baru recorded the highest number of cases last week, with 173 or 62.9 per cent of the state total, followed by Kulai with 70 cases (25.5 per cent).
The remaining cases were reported in Kluang and Pontian (seven each), Segamat (six), Kota Tinggi (four), Muar (three), Mersing and Batu Pahat (two each), and Tangkak (one).
Ling said 17 new dengue outbreak localities were reported during the week, comprising 10 in Johor Baru, six in Kulai and one in Kluang.
The cumulative number of outbreak localities reached 1,489 this year, compared with 532 during the corresponding period last year, an increase of 180 per cent.
He said enforcement operations had resulted in 5,338 compounds worth RM2.669 million being issued this year, of which 76.19 per cent had been paid.
However, inspections continued to uncover potential mosquito breeding sites inside and outside homes, indicating that residents were still not doing enough to eliminate stagnant water.
Ling called on the public to spend at least 10 minutes checking and eliminating potential Aedes breeding grounds at home and workplaces, including containers that could collect stagnant water.
Residents were also advised to cover water storage containers, remove stagnant water and scrub containers to eliminate mosquito larvae.
Schools were encouraged to organise regular clean-up activities, while school bus operators and drivers were advised to use aerosol sprays inside buses before morning and afternoon student journeys.

2cfad095cbd4c757: KUALA LUMPUR: The Works Ministry received only about half of the RM5 billion to RM6 billion it sought for road maintenance, Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan told the Dewan Rakyat.
He said the ministry received RM2.68 billion in 2026, while RM2.59 billion was approved for 2027.
Ahmad said the shortfall was among the reasons road maintenance and resurfacing works nationwide could not be carried out to the extent required.
"When honourable members raise the issue of roads that have not been fully paved or need resurfacing, one of the causes is budget constraints.
"It is not that the ministry did not apply. We applied for between RM5 billion and RM6 billion, but received only about RM2.5 billion, which is half of what is needed," he said.
He was winding up for the Works Ministry during the committee-stage debate on its 2027 Budget allocation.
Ahmad said the Finance Ministry and the Economy Ministry should take note of the shortfall to ensure actual maintenance needs were considered when allocations were drawn up.

"I do not intend to blame any party, but it is important for the Finance and Economy ministries to look at the overall budget needs that are very important to the people, especially road maintenance," he said.
He said although the Works Ministry received the highest development allocation among the 28 ministries, the amount was still insufficient to meet all its needs, particularly road maintenance.

Ahmad said the ministry's road maintenance allocation was RM1.6 billion in 2021, RM1.17 billion in 2022, RM1.71 billion in 2023, RM2.39 billion in 2024, RM2.99 billion in 2025 and RM2.68 billion in 2026.

On alternative approaches to road paving, he said the ministry, through the Public Works Department's Centre of Excellence for Engineering and Technology (CREaTE), was researching more durable paving materials.
These included mixtures using crumb rubber, rubber from gloves and discarded plastic.
However, he said the cost of using such materials remained higher than conventional paving because they were not yet widely used.
"Still, when we want to implement it, the cost of the materials is rather higher than ordinary paving. That is another constraint.
"However, if the allocation is sufficient, all these matters can be resolved," he said.
b243af12c12850ea: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Malaysia aspires to be more than just a participant in the energy transition landscape, but instead emerge as a leader, technology owner and creator of opportunities in the green energy sector through the development of local expertise, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.

The Energy Transition and Water Transformation minister said energy transition was not just an environmental agenda, but also a catalyst for economic growth that could create high-value employment opportunities and enhance the competitiveness of local industries.

Fadillah said this after officiating the Gading Kencana Solar Farm under the Corporate Green Power Programme (CGPP), which was developed through a strategic collaboration between local renewable energy company Gading Kencana Sdn Bhd and global semiconductor company Intel.

"We do not merely want to be participants in the energy transition, but emerge as leaders, technology owners and creators of opportunities in the country’s green energy landscape,” he said in a Facebook post.
Fadillah said the 43-megawatt peak (MWp) solar farm demonstrated that the country’s energy transition was no longer just an aspiration, but was becoming a reality.
He said the project also demonstrated the ability of local companies to gain the trust of international investors through a combination of investment, innovation and expertise.

He said the achievement was particularly commendable as it reflected the ability of Bumiputera companies to expand their participation in high-technology industries, develop expertise and compete internationally.
Meanwhile, Intel had entered into a 15-year long-term agreement to purchase 53,000 Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) annually through the collaboration.
He said the commitment reflected international investors’ confidence in the potential and capabilities of Malaysia’s clean energy ecosystem.

"I hope that the success of Gading Kencana, one of the pioneers of Malaysia’s large-scale solar industry for more than two decades, would inspire more local companies to explore new opportunities, master technologies and develop their own capabilities.

"Indeed, energy transition is a shared commitment and responsibility. Our success is measured not only by the amount of energy generated or the value of investments secured, but by the benefits we can deliver to the people,” he said. — Bernama

d6449b24b1fa082d: KUANTAN: The inquest into the death of an Orang Asli man in police custody at Pekan police headquarters two years ago began today, with a lawyer representing his family questioning whether he could have been saved through immediate intervention.

Counsel Datuk Bob Arumugam, who is holding a watching brief for the family, told the Coroner's Court that there was a 24-minute gap between the time Norazman Me was seen attempting to hang himself using his lock-up attire at 1.46am on May 4, 2024, and when the officer on duty realised what had happened at 2.10am.
He said closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed that the incident went unnoticed for 24 minutes, raising questions about whether anyone was monitoring the surveillance cameras at the time.

"From the CCTV image, there was a 24-minute gap during which nobody appeared to be monitoring the footage. Could he have been brought down immediately if the incident had been noticed earlier? He might still have been alive," he said during cross-examination.

Earlier, Pekan police chief Superintendent Mohd Zaidi Mat Zin, the first witness to testify, explained 20 CCTV screenshots captured at the police headquarters, including footage of the lock-up area and the cell where Norazman was found.

Deputy public prosecutor Khamisah Ismail, who is conducting the inquest, had asked Zaidi to identify the individuals shown in the images and explain the sequence of events, including the timestamps leading up to the final image showing Norazman's body being taken out of the lock-up around 7am.

On safety measures introduced after the incident, Zaidi said officers on duty, who were previously required to inspect the lock-up once an hour, had been instructed to conduct rounds every 30 minutes.
"We no longer keep an accused person alone in a cell. Instead, we place two people in each cell," he said.
Norazman's family had sought answers after being informed that the 25-year-old father of one was found dead in his cell at Pekan police headquarters on May 4, 2024.
He was arrested on suspicion of vehicle theft on May 1 and remanded until May 6 after testing positive for morphine.
A post-mortem conducted at Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital here recorded the cause of death as hanging.
On Oct 24, 2024, Bukit Aman's Integrity and Standards Compliance Department said it would hand over the investigation findings into Norazman's death to the coroner.
The inquest will continue on Jan 27 and 28 next year before Coroner Sazlina Safie.
Also present in court today were Norazman's parents, Me Kingking, 60, and Noriah Hitam, 53, and one of his siblings.

Tempers flared when Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) interjected, claiming that Rayer's objection also appeared to insult the unity government. Rayer responded loudly, telling him not to interrupt.
Ahmad said he might have got carried away with the pantun but insisted that he had not mentioned PH. Ramli then ruled on the use of the word.
"My ruling on the word 'kencing', the word has nothing to do with anyone as such, but in this context it is unparliamentary," he said.
Ahmad continued speaking without explicitly withdrawing the word. When Rayer asked Ramli to make him do so, Ahmad asked whether it was only that particular word that was objectionable.
Ramli said the intention behind the word was what mattered.
"Mr Speaker says withdraw the word 'kencing'. Okay. I withdraw," Ahmad said.
The exchange followed Ahmad's earlier remarks on calls by MPs to abolish tolls during the debate on the Works Ministry's 2027 Budget allocation.
"We have not promised to abolish tolls. We made no promises. So whoever made the promises must answer," he said.
He said abolishing tolls would require an estimated RM400 billion to take over all 34 toll highways, which are operated under 28 concessions.
"Does the government have RM400 billion to take over all 34 toll highways? I ask. RM400 billion is about a year's budget, you know," he said.

ef9820b5dc71bc04: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan disaran memperluas pemberian diskaun tambang perkhidmatan Laluan Rel Pantai Timur (ECRL) kepada golongan B40, khususnya penerima Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) dan mereka yang berdaftar dengan eKasih.
Shaharizukirnain Abd Kadir (PN-Setiu) berkata, cadangan itu adalah bagi memastikan kemudahan itu mampu dinikmati lebih ramai rakyat berpendapatan rendah.
Tambahnya, jika kerajaan boleh menyediakan diskaun 50% bagi warga emas dan orang kurang upaya (OKU), selain tambang khas bagi pelajar, golongan B40 juga wajar diberikan pertimbangan sama.

“Apa salahnya jika kerajaan beri diskaun kepada penumpang dalam kalangan B40, mereka yang berdaftar dengan eKasih dan penerima STR?” katanya ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027 peringkat jawatankuasa Kementerian Pengangkutan.
Beliau turut meminta kerajaan menjelaskan bila pakej perjalanan keluarga akan dilaksanakan agar orang ramai dapat menikmati tambang lebih murah, khususnya keluarga besar.
Sebagai contoh, katanya, tambang perjalanan ECRL dari Gombak, Kuala Lumpur, ke Setiu, Terengganu, ialah RM107 sehala bagi seorang dewasa atau RM214 untuk perjalanan pergi dan balik.
Kos itu akan meningkat bagi keluarga yang mempunyai ramai ahli, sekali gus menjadi beban kepada golongan berpendapatan rendah, terutama penduduk di Pantai Timur, jelasnya.

Diumumkan bulan lepas bahawa tambang sehala bagi ECRL dari Gombak ke Kota Bharu bermula RM125 untuk perkhidmatan transit dan RM147 untuk perkhidmatan ekspres, dengan tiket boleh didapati mulai pertengahan bulan ini.

Penumpang kanak-kanak berusia dua hingga 12 tahun, warga emas berusia 60 tahun ke atas, pemegang kad orang kurang upaya (OKU) serta pesara kerajaan akan menerima diskaun 50% bagi tambang, manakala pelajar berusia 13 hingga 24 tahun pula akan menerima diskaun 40%.

Menurut Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL), perkhidmatan transit akan berhenti di setiap stesen, manakala perkhidmatan ekspres hanya berhenti di empat stesen utama, iaitu Gombak, KotaSAS, Kuala Terengganu dan Kota Bharu.
MRL memaklumkan, mekanisme harga dinamik akan digunakan, dengan harga tiket berbeza-beza mengikut waktu perjalanan, permintaan dan ketersediaan tempat duduk.
Katanya, kerajaan telah meluluskan cadangan pelaksanaan tambang itu pada 16 Okt, menjelang perancangan pelancaran perkhidmatan penumpang komersial pada pertengahan Disember.
24add1d46f301e0b: PETALING JAYA: Kumpulan Wang Simpanan Pekerja (KWSP) mencatatkan pendapatan pelaburan RM83.32 bilion bagi tempoh sembilan bulan pertama berakhir pada 30 Sept, iaitu meningkat 30% berbanding RM63.99 bilion dalam tempoh sama pada 2025.
Dana simpanan persaraan itu menjelaskan jumlah pendapatan pelaburan bagi suku ketiga 2026 itu meningkat tiga peratus kepada RM25.82 bilion, berbanding RM25.07 bilion pada suku sama tahun lalu.

Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif KWSP Ahmad Zulqarnain Onn, berkata keputusan bagi tempoh sembilan bulan pertama itu mencerminkan daya tahan portfolio pelaburan yang pelbagai dan kesinambungan strategi seperti dilaksanakan pada suku sebelumnya.

“Kami menyaksikan pertumbuhan pendapatan yang lebih sederhana pada suku ketiga, dan trend ini dijangka berterusan pada suku keempat berikutan kelemahan dalam pasaran ekuiti global serta peningkatan hasil dalam pasaran bon.
“Pada awal suku ini, risiko berkaitan tahap pinjaman kerajaan, inflasi yang berterusan dan penilaian saham berkaitan kecerdasan buatan (AI) semakin meningkat,” katanya menurut Bernama.

Ahmad Zulqarnain berkata, perkembangan itu mendorong KWSP terus berdisiplin dalam menguruskan portfolio, mengimbangi peluang pelaburan dan risiko yang muncul, selain kekal fokus bagi menjana pulangan mampan dalam tempoh jangka panjang serta memelihara kesejahteraan persaraan ahli.

Menurut KWSP, pendapatan ekuiti meningkat tiga peratus kepada RM17.41 bilion pada suku ketiga 2026, berbanding RM16.95 bilion pada suku yang sama tahun lalu, merangkumi 67% daripada jumlah pendapatan pelaburan bagi suku tersebut.

Selain itu, pasaran ekuiti global kekal berdaya tahan sepanjang suku tersebut, disokong oleh pendapatan korporat yang kukuh, pelaburan berterusan dalam tema berkaitan AI dan keadaan ekonomi yang secara umumnya menggalakkan.
“Keadaan ini memberikan peluang kepada pengurus dana KWSP untuk mengurus portfolio secara aktif dan menjana nilai, sekali gus menyumbang kepada peningkatan pendapatan ekuiti,” menurut KWSP.
Bagi instrumen pendapatan tetap, KWSP memaklumkan ia menyumbang RM7.12 bilion atau 28% daripada jumlah pendapatan pelaburan pada suku ketiga 2026.

“Walaupun peningkatan hasil di pasaran utama memberi tekanan terhadap penilaian portfolio bon sepanjang suku tersebut, pelaburan pendapatan tetap terus menjana pendapatan yang berdaya tahan dan menyumbang kestabilan kepada keseluruhan portfolio,” menurut dana itu lagi.

Menurut KWSP, infrastruktur dan hartanah mencatatkan pendapatan RM890 juta pada suku ketiga 2026, manakala instrumen pasaran wang mencatatkan keuntungan RM400 juta, seiring dengan jangkaan pulangan bagi kelas aset masing-masing.
Setakat 30 Sept, jumlah aset pelaburan sebanyak RM1.55 trilion, dengan 38% daripadanya dilaburkan di peringkat global.
KWSP juga memaklumkan bahawa pelaburan antarabangsa menjana pendapatan RM13.68 bilion, merangkumi 53% daripada jumlah pendapatan pelaburan bagi suku tersebut.
Jumlah pendapatan pelaburan bagi simpanan konvensional dan simpanan shariah pula masing-masing berjumlah RM21.39 bilion dan RM4.43 bilion.
Mengenai keahlian, KWSP menyatakan bahawa ia mendaftar kira-kira 659,000 ahli baharu bagi sembilan bulan pertama 2026, menjadikan jumlah keahlian kepada lebih 18.6 juta.
Daripada jumlah itu, jumlah ahli aktif meningkat kepada 11.2 juta, dengan nisbah ahli aktif kepada tidak aktif bertambah baik kepada 60:40.
Dalam pada itu, jumlah sumbangan meningkat 9.34% kepada RM30.44 bllion pada suku ketiga 2026, berbanding RM27.84 bilion bagi suku sama tahun lalu.

Menurut KWSP lagi, jumlah caruman sukarela juga meningkat kepada RM18.27 bilion pada tempoh sembilan bulan pertama tahun ini, sekali gus menunjukkan kesedaran berterusan ahli untuk menambah simpanan persaraan mereka melebihi caruman mandatori.

9f3294f3d4e429be: BANGKOK, Nov 16 — A Thai court denied an attempt on Monday by former leader Thaksin Shinawatra to pause the seizure of his assets over a disputed tax bill of more than US$500 million (RM2 billion).
The Supreme Court ordered the ex-prime minister – one of Thailand’s richest people – last November to pay back taxes over the 2006 sale of shares in his telecoms firm.

Thaksin then sought a temporary injunction against the Revenue Department to stop it from seizing his assets to pay the bill, which the tax court said was around THB17.5 billion (around US$515 million).
The request was dismissed, according to a court statement on Monday. A mediation between Thaksin and the Revenue Department before the tax court is set for December.
Thaksin, 77, argued in court last month that he had already settled the bill for the tax-free sale of Shin Corp to Singapore’s Temasek Holdings.
The 2006 deal, which netted the Shinawatra family a US$1.9 billion windfall, sparked protests and became a lightning rod for opposition to Thaksin’s government.
He was ousted in a coup later that year and went into exile for more than a decade, during which time he was convicted of corruption.
Thaksin was arrested when he returned in 2023 but sent to hospital and then freed. He finally saw the inside of a jail last year, serving eight months before his release in May.
The Shinawatra clan has for two decades been a key foe of Thailand’s pro-military, pro-royalty elite, who view their populist brand of politics as a threat to the traditional social order.
However, the political dynasty has faced a series of setbacks, including the court-ordered removal of Thaksin’s daughter, Paetongtarn, as prime minister in August 2025 over an ethics breach.
Their Pheu Thai party also had its worst election result in February, slipping to third place, but was still included in the ruling coalition of conservative Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. — AFP

abb0e23108d956a4: HOLLYWOOD, Nov 16 — Hollywood royalty Glenn Close and Ridley Scott both received an honorary Oscar on Sunday, the first golden statues of their decades-long careers, at a lavish gala bringing together industry elites.
Screen legend Close, 79, has been tipped for Academy Awards eight times during her five-decade career, including for her roles in “Fatal Attraction” and “Dangerous Liaisons.”
British director Ridley Scott, 88, known for box-office hits including “Alien,” “Blade Runner” and “Gladiator,” is a nine-time nominee but had also never won the award.
The honorary Oscars, awarded annually by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, celebrate cinema legends for their careers and contributions to the film industry.
US actor John Malkovich, who is tipped for Oscars glory for his role in dark comedy “Wild Horse Nine,” introduced Close as “a friend and a treasured colleague.”
“She is a true master,” said Malkovich, who starred alongside Close as the arch seducer in “Dangerous Liaisons.”
“Glenn is unafraid to go there, and I love that about her.”
Close, who dedicated the award to her daughter, earned a standing ovation.

“As an outsider, I have never worried about whether I was going to win or not, though some years I thought I might have a chance,” said the actress, who earned her first nomination for 1983 hit “The World According to Garp.”
“I have always felt that the great honour is to be in the room,” she added.
Three-time Best Director nominee Scott received his gong from Matt Damon, who paid tribute to the master of the modern screen epic.
“It is about time we all saw him with an Academy Award in his hand,” said Damon, who worked with Scott on 2015 box office smash “The Martian.”
The director did not attend the event at the Ray Dolby Ballroom in the heart of Hollywood, but expressed his gratitude in a pre-recorded video.
Director Christopher Nolan and actors including Tom Holland, Charlize Theron, Olivia Wilde and Penelope Cruz were among dozens of star attendees.
The 17th edition of the awards, which precedes the Golden Globes in January and the Oscars in March, also paid tribute to legendary animator Floyd Norman.

“On occasion, even movies have a happy ending,” the 91-year-old said.

3411c497853951d7: From Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri
There is something more dangerous in politics than losing an election: winning one without understanding why.
The Melaka state election should be a wake-up call for both Pakatan Harapan (PH) and the Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional (BN-PN) alliance.
BN-PN may celebrate its overwhelming victory, while PH may console itself with retaining a loyal support base. But beneath the celebrations and disappointments lies an uncomfortable reality.

PH has yet to demonstrate that it can significantly expand its appeal among Malay voters. BN-PN, meanwhile, has yet to prove that Malay political consolidation can translate into broader national acceptance.
Let the numbers speak.
In 2021, PH secured 114,457 votes, representing nearly 35.8% of the popular vote. In 2026, its tally increased to 143,273, but its vote share declined to 29.3%.
PH gained almost 29,000 votes, yet lost 6.5 percentage points of electoral support.
That is not an insignificant distinction.
PH is not necessarily losing its existing voters. It is losing the race to win over new ones.
More embarrassingly, all four seats won by PH went to DAP. PKR and Amanah failed to secure even a single constituency.

This raises an uncomfortable question: how can a coalition led by a Malay prime minister, supported by Malay ministers and commanding federal power, struggle so badly to translate that leadership into electoral success in Malay-majority constituencies?
PKR must ask whether its reformist identity still inspires confidence beyond its traditional supporters.
Amanah must explain why its supposedly progressive Islamic alternative has struggled to establish meaningful electoral traction.
A political party cannot survive indefinitely by reminding voters of what it once fought for. Eventually, voters want to know what it has delivered.
Reformasi cannot remain a historical slogan. It must become a measurable improvement in people's lives.
DAP should not celebrate too comfortably either.
Preliminary turnout estimates suggest that nearly 78% of Malay voters participated, compared with 59% of Chinese voters and 58% of Indian voters.
Although Chinese support for PH among those who voted appears relatively resilient, the weaker participation should worry DAP.
Chinese voters are not PH's permanent electoral fixed deposit.
They have expectations concerning education, economic opportunities, institutional reform and fair governance.
Fear of PAS may motivate some voters. But fear is not a substitute for trust, and disappointment can be expressed through silence at the ballot box.
Now consider BN-PN.
In 2021, BN and PN collectively received 200,472 votes while contesting separately. In 2026, their combined tally reached 308,668.
That represents an impressive 54% increase in absolute votes.
However, their combined popular vote share moved only marginally, from nearly 62.7% to 63.1%.
The alliance achieved a landslide in seats without achieving a comparable breakthrough in its combined share of the electorate.
This is not to diminish its victory. It is to distinguish electoral consolidation from a genuine expansion of political appeal.
And here lies BN-PN's greatest contradiction.

If its political identity increasingly revolves around Malay nationalism and religious conservatism, how does it intend to persuade Chinese, Indian, Sabah and Sarawak voters that their interests will be equally protected?
MCA and MIC may have won constituencies, but isolated victories do not automatically demonstrate a nationwide recovery of non-Malay confidence.
If Umno's ambition is merely to become more Malay than PAS, what exactly is MCA's future role? A political partner or a decorative guest at victory celebrations?
Defending Malay interests should never require making other communities feel politically expendable.
Malaysia's future cannot be secured by making one community believe that another community's progress represents its own defeat.
So what should PH do?
First, abandon the assumption that government performance automatically produces electoral loyalty.
I would propose an independent, constituency-level voter confidence audit, particularly among rural Malays, younger voters and the lower-middle-income population.
Ask those who rejected PH one simple question: what would convince you to reconsider?
Then publish measurable commitments on wages, housing, employment and living costs, with progress assessed every six months.

Second, PH must rebuild its political language. Ordinary Malaysians do not wake up thinking about coalition arithmetic. They wake up worrying about groceries, school expenses, wages and their children's future.
Third, stop treating criticism as hostility. Sometimes the harshest critics are identifying problems that loyal supporters refuse to acknowledge.
BN-PN should undertake an equally uncomfortable exercise: test its policies and political messaging among voters who do not share its ethnic or religious identity.

If the alliance cannot convince a substantial number of non-Malays that they have a secure future under its leadership, it risks becoming a powerful regional force with a national credibility problem.
The elections in Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka offer valuable lessons, but they are not a reliable national forecast.
Umno should remember what happened after its victories in Melaka in 2021 and Johor in 2022.
Confidence turned into pressure for an early general election. Yet GE15 delivered BN its worst parliamentary performance up to that point.
Winning several states does not mean the keys to Putrajaya are already in your pocket.
Malaysia's electoral landscape is shaped by different demographics, local personalities, regional identities and economic expectations.
There is another reality politicians rarely admit openly: patronage, financial assistance and personal obligations remain influential in electoral politics.
Malaysians understand the saying, "orang berbudi kita berbahasa" ... kindness deserves appreciation.
But gratitude should never become political indebtedness.
A RM100 handout may ease household expenses today. A poor government can impose economic costs on an entire generation.

Ultimately, PH must learn to attract new voters rather than merely retain old supporters. BN-PN must learn to build confidence across communities rather than simply consolidate Malay political strength.
Neither side can claim to have solved Malaysia's political future.
An election determines who governs for five years. But the consequences of choosing the wrong leaders may be inherited for five generations.
Perhaps that is the greatest tragedy of Malaysian politics — our politicians are obsessed with counting the seats needed to capture power.
The people should be counting the price their children may eventually pay for it.
Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri is an analyst with Global Asia Consulting.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.

2c5ddaa66400b1d6: MOSCOW: Russia on Monday criticised Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky for revealing Washington had proposed that Kyiv cede land for Nato membership as part of a possible peace deal with Moscow.
The Kremlin did not confirm the proposal had been made or comment on it. But Moscow has long opposed Ukraine joining the US-led military alliance.

"We continue to maintain our position that it is inadvisable to disclose details of the discussions taking place between us and the Americans in the interests of the peace process," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters, including AFP.

Zelensky had told journalists on Friday that the offer had been made by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who last week held talks in Abu Dhabi with both sides before separate meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky.
"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky said.
Kyiv has long pushed for Nato membership hoping its mutual defence clauses will be a guarantee against a future Russian attack.
But Moscow has for years railed against new countries joining Nato – believing it was promised by the United States that that alliance would not move closer to its borders.
Since it launched its full-scale offensive on Ukraine in 2022, both Sweden and Finland – which has a 1,300km (800-mile) border with Russia - have joined Nato.

71bfc93bc2f23df1: FRANKFURT: The European Central Bank warned Monday of growing risks from an "abrupt repricing" in markets and big losses if investor sentiment about artificial intelligence sours.
The comments from the ECB's vice president Boris Vujcic add to mounting concerns about the sector as investors increasingly question whether massive AI spending will pay off.

Jitters and market swings have been fuelled by the scandal that toppled Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang last week, and the Democratic wins in the US midterm elections that could spark greater oversight of AI technologies.
Vujcic said the "rapid expansion of AI is creating new challenges for financial stability" in the 21-nation eurozone.
"A reassessment of the AI narrative may trigger an abrupt repricing in markets and significant valuation losses," he warned in a speech in Frankfurt.
Initial public offering volumes relative to US GDP are on track to exceed the levels seen at the height of the dot-com boom of the late 1990s, Vujcic noted.
Shares in the AI titan Anthropic are expected to start trading on Wall Street on Thursday, in what could be the second-largest IPO in history.
"Historically, such surges have often coincided with market peaks, pointing to the risk of excessive investor optimism," Vujcic said.
Market falls after the Democratic sweep of Congress in the US midterms, which stoked regulatory concerns, "serve as a reminder to remain cautious about AI valuations," he said.
An AI-linked market crash represents a major risk for the eurozone because investment funds in the region had become more exposed to the sector, he added.
022548738f84fd7f: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) has allocated RM3.362 million to strengthen stray dog management nationwide through financial assistance to local authorities, awareness campaigns and the construction of adoption centres.

Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said the allocation included a one-off grant of RM902,471 for local authorities to purchase euthanasia medication and equipment to capture stray dogs.
She said the allocation comprised RM58,841 for 28 local authorities in 2021, RM65,630 for 29 in 2022, RM140,000 for 31 in 2025 and RM638,000 for 71 local authorities in 2026.

"…we have also allocated funds for the Stray Animal Management Campaign, which was launched in 2024. A total of RM180,000 was allocated that year, followed by RM130,000 in 2025 and RM150,000 this year, bringing the total to RM460,000,” she said during a Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

Her response followed a question from Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) on efforts to improve the sustainable management of stray dogs nationwide and the ministry's provision of financial assistance to local authorities for stray animal control.

KPKT had also provided RM2 million this year for two adoption centres overseen by Johor Bahru City Council and Sandakan Municipal Council, through its Local Government Department (JKT), Aiman Athirah said.
On the approach to managing stray dogs, she said the ministry followed a four-pronged policy known as trap, reclaim, rehome and dispose.

"Since September, the ministry has directed all local authorities to step up enforcement efforts, including conducting checks on dog ownership and licensing in residential areas to ensure owners comply with the dog licensing by-laws in force in their respective jurisdictions,” she said.
She said local authorities nationwide received 45,804 complaints about stray dog disturbances last year, and 24,195 operations resulted in 80,412 stray dogs being caught.

"Of these, some were handed over to the Department of Veterinary Services, while others were reclaimed by their owners or adopted through dog adoption programmes. These figures reflect KPKT's and local authorities' continued commitment to controlling and managing stray dogs,” she said.

She said the ministry acknowledged the proposal to introduce a more comprehensive national framework for managing stray animals, but any move to strengthen existing mechanisms would be undertaken in phases involving multiple agencies.

She added that KPKT welcomed suggestions from non-governmental organisations on improving stray animal management nationwide, particularly through adoption programmes, shelter facilities and public education.

c149d6ef361bb5d6: TASEK GELUGOR: Enforcement officers seized 27,000 bottles of hair dye worth RM1.08 million after uncovering the misuse of Malaysian halal logos.
Penang Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) director S. Jegan said the raid on a rented warehouse here followed three weeks of intelligence gathering and public complaints.
Two warehouse workers in their 30s, a woman and a Chinese national, were detained to assist in investigations.
Jegan said the company had imported the hair dye from China and sold it exclusively through social media and e-commerce platforms, including TikTok, Shopee and Lazada.
"In six months of operations, they managed to sell nearly 600,000 units at RM40 per box.
"This is a major concern because hair dye is widely used, including by the elderly. It was a 'hot killer item' in the warehouse," he told reporters at the scene.

Jegan said investigations found that the product packaging displayed a generic halal logo without a valid serial number, while promotional videos featured influential affiliates and even religious figures displaying a Malaysian halal certificate belonging to another company.

"It is a clear-cut offence as the product does not have valid Malaysian halal certification from the Malaysian Islamic Development Department (Jakim) or any State Islamic Religious Council," he added.
The case is being investigated under the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 (Act 730).
Upon conviction, individuals face a fine of up to RM1 million, a jail term of up to three years or both, while companies face a fine of up to RM5 million.
Jegan advised consumers to verify halal claims directly through the Jakim portal before purchasing products online, rather than relying solely on social media affiliates.

Explaining the mechanics behind the gate rejections, the ticketing firm revealed that primary buyers who resold their passes subsequently attempted to gain entry using duplicate copies of the same tickets.
“The original purchasers also attempted to attend the events using the same tickets.

The company strongly advised ticket holders against sharing account credentials, posting unobscured ticket screenshots online, or clicking suspicious links that could compromise personal devices.

The controversy underscores the persistent challenge of predatory scalping confronting Malaysia as it cements its reputation as a premier regional concert hub. 1b0140990325da00: Omaxian OS is only at version 0.1, but it already takes a distinctly unconventional route through the Linux desktop.
The brand-new Linux desktop distro describes itself as "the Omarchy desktop on X11 — as a shell for your Debian, or as a whole OS." That's not quite the impression that we came away with, though.

Like most distros, Omaxian is available as an ISO file you can install and use. Alternatively, Omaxian Shell can be installed on an existing Debian-family distro without replacing the underlying operating system.

The OS release is codenamed "Trans-Siberian Shaman," and the GitHub project repository shows work going back just a few weeks. No LLM coding assistant is credited on the project page, but we looked inside some of the test scripts, and as well as being verbose and hard to read, they also credit "Grok Bot." Omarchy itself is of course built with LLM assistance, and as we reported last month, so is the new Daemonarchy FreeBSD-based desktop project.

Omaxian is styled after Omarchy, and it includes some of the same tools – and optional support for LLMs – but it's not based on the same tech. Instead of Arch, it's based on Devuan 6, the current version of the systemd-free fork of Debian. Omaxian eschews Hyprland, and indeed Wayland altogether: it opts for an X11 tiling window manager – in this case, i3. i3 first appeared in 2009, so it's been around much longer than Hyprland. Omaxian's configuration also understands familiar keystrokes such as Alt+F4 to close a window. For us, that's a significant usability win.

The window manager isn't running on top of X.org. Omaxian uses the 2025 fork, the new XLibre X11 server. This is a controversial project led by a controversial developer, which will be enough for some people to want to avoid Omaxian as a whole. The latest release of GhostBSD uses XLibre too, though.

Way back in 2021, The Register reported on Omarchy creator David Heinemeier Hansson's company banning political discussions, and things have only got more vexed since. Just as DHH has attracted some notoriety for his now right-wing views, his Linux is similarly opinionated. If the associations surrounding Omarchy and XLibre put you off, Omaxian's combination of the two probably won't win you over.

The flipside is that if you don't care about the political views, but are interested in the idea of a tiling environment set up for power users who embrace LLM coding assistance, then you might like Omaxian. The full distro trades Arch, Wayland, and systemd for a Devuan base, X11, and sysvinit, with APT handling conventional packages. Flatpaks and AppImages are available too.

We tried Omaxian in VirtualBox, but we experienced frequent display corruption. We must give it this: the interface is slightly easier to navigate than Hyprland. One touch that we did like is that if you get tired of the tiling stuff and want to switch back to something more conventional, then Xfce is also installed in the background. Xfce provides Omaxian with a file manager and other accessories, but you can just choose Xfce from the login screen and find yourself back in a simple, familiar, classic desktop environment.

Omaxian is not the sort of environment we're looking for. This vulture isn't a developer and doesn't use LLMs for anything at all. However, lots of people are looking for something like that, as demonstrated by Omarchy's sponsorship. But it's bold, colorful, and significantly different from the mainstream, and that is the sort of thing we do like to see. ®

a6d0a51e1903e5ed: PETALING JAYA: Terengganu menteri besar Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar says the state government will not sack Bersatu representatives from the executive council, claiming that the administration is still running smoothly.

“At this time, everything is running quite smoothly. There may be some differences (in circumstances) between us and the Kelantan government, we’ll see,” he told reporters at the state assembly building today.
Last week, the Kelantan government removed state Bersatu chief Kamarudin Nor as an executive councillor.
Kamarudin’s removal followed a breakdown in relations between PAS and Bersatu after the Islamic party announced on June 8 that it was ending their political cooperation.

The Terengganu government currently has one Bersatu exco member – Kijal assemblyman Razali Idris – and three Bersatu deputy exco members: Husaimi Hussin (Hulu Besut), Yusop Majid (Permaisuri) and Zawawi Ismail (Telemung).
On Oct 1, Razali hinted at leaving Bersatu for a new party, more than a month after relinquishing his post as Terengganu Bersatu chairman.
Samsuri said action may be taken if issues arise among the deputy exco members.
“If there are problems among them, we’ll take action. What kind of action? We’ll have to wait and see,” he said.
'PN election wins boost ties with BN'

Samsuri, who is also the Perikatan Nasional (PN) chairman, said PN’s success in Saturday's Melaka election, together with its performance in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, had built a strong foundation for cooperation with Barisan Nasional in coming elections, including the 16th general election.
He said no discussions had been held between the two coalitions on the Terengganu election, which must be held by Nov 23, 2028, or any federal election plan.
“We will sort this out one by one. We will first figure out how to contribute to Melaka’s government. Once everything is stabilised, we will then begin discussions on other states,” he said.
Bersatu, while still technically a component party of PN, has seen relations with the coalition deteriorate after its falling-out with lynchpin party PAS on June 8.

The fallout with PAS led Bersatu to improve relations with Pakatan Harapan, including by signing a confidence and supply agreement in October pledging support for Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s government.
8010d817f46d0708: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Hockey Confederation (MHC) welcomes and fully supports the decision by the Youth and Sports Ministry and the National Sports Council (NSC) to increase the incentives under the National Sports Incentive Scheme (Shakam).
For each member of a team that wins a gold medal at the Asian Games, Asian Para Games, or Commonwealth Games, the incentive has been raised from RM15,000 to RM40,000.
For silver medals, the individual incentive has increased from RM8,000 to RM20,000, while for bronze medals, it has risen from RM4,000 to RM10,000.
These new rates apply to all teams, regardless of the number of members, and include medalists from 2026.
This marks the first adjustment to team incentive rates since they were established in 2002.
MHC considers this move both timely and fair to athletes competing in team events.
In the context of hockey, this improvement directly benefits the 20 players on the national men's hockey squad who secured a silver medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.

Under the previous rates, each player on a silver-medal-winning team received RM8,000, compared to RM40,000 for an individual silver medalist. With this enhancement, the amount increases to RM20,000 per person.

In total, the 20 national hockey athletes will receive an additional payout amounting to RM240,000, while the coaches will receive an additional RM48,000 under the Coaches' Incentive Scheme (SGAR), bringing the total additional allocation to RM288,000.
MHC expresses its deepest appreciation to the minister, Dr Taufiq Johari, for his swift action.
MHC president Datuk Seri Subahan Kamal said success in hockey is the result of a collective effort, requiring the commitment, sacrifice, and dedication of every individual within the team.

"Hockey is not a sport built upon the brilliance of a single individual. It is a team sport, where every member plays a vital role in determining success in any given tournament. No goals are scored and no victories are achieved without the contribution of every player.

"This initiative comes at a highly significant juncture, crucial for sustaining the players' motivation, fighting spirit, and competitiveness as they prepare for the 2027 SEA Games and the qualification campaign for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games," he said.

MHC believes that improvements in rewards and recognition are not only essential for retaining experienced players within the national squad, but also serve as a catalyst to attract the younger generation to the sport.
675abcedd526662f: KUALA LUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd, through an 80:20 joint venture (JV) with Taiwan-based Feng Shun Construction Co Ltd, has secured a contract worth NT$21.02 billion (approximately RM2.61 billion) to undertake the design and construction of the Keelung Underground Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) project in Taiwan.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the engineering and construction company said the Department of Rapid Transit Systems, New Taipei City Government awarded the contract on Nov 16, 2026.
"The project comprises 2.4 km of underground works located across Nangang District (Taipei City) to Xizhi District (New Taipei City), including two underground stations.
"It is expected to be completed within 7.4 years," the company said.
It said the project incorporates environmental, social and governance principles through the use of eco-friendly materials, energy-efficient systems and sustainable construction practices.
'The project is expected to contribute positively to its revenue and earnings for the financial year ending July 31, 2027, until its completion," it added.
6686af4690bd9e09: KUALA LUMPUR: Eco World Development Group Bhd (EcoWorld) has signed an agreement with Permodalan Darul Ta'zim Sdn Bhd (PDT) to explore supplying renewable electricity and reclaimed water to data centres and industrial parks in Johor.

Under the agreement, PDT will facilitate the supply of green utilities through PDT Energy Sdn Bhd and Johor Special Water Sdn Bhd (JSW) to EcoWorld's industrial and data centre customers, subject to pricing and other commercial terms to be finalised.

EcoWorld will promote these utilities to its network of green consumers and provide the utility suppliers with information on customers' anticipated consumption, demand forecasts and timelines, subject to their consent where required.
EcoWorld said its Quantum and Eco Business Parks have a growing network of eligible green energy consumers and other potential customers.
PDT, the Johor government's strategic investment arm, is responsible for implementing the Johor Green Development Policy 2030 and leading efforts to supply green utilities in the state.

Through PDT Energy and its joint venture partners, PDT plans to supply renewable electricity and renewable energy certificates to eligible consumers under the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme and other potential customers.
JSW, meanwhile, holds exclusive rights to supply raw water, treated effluent, reclaimed water and alternative water for industrial use in Johor.

"By seamlessly connecting the supply dynamics of green utilities with clear projections of actual demand, the collaboration agreement supports the state's aims to drive green investments and technology adoption while encouraging industries to improve energy efficiency and optimising the use of water resources.

"Together, these efforts will help sustain Johor's momentum in high value economic growth, while ensuring EcoWorld's industrial projects continue to be supported by reliable, efficient and sustainable utilities," EcoWorld said.
4360f308a3a913fa: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 —The government does not plan to create any new economic corridor in the Wang Kelian area, but will strengthen the framework for the Northern Corridor Region (NCER) and the Border Economic Zone (BEZ), which is being finalised, the Economy Ministry said.

Its Deputy Minister Datuk Mohd Shahar Abdullah said this approach avoids duplicating functions with the Northern Corridor Implementation Authority (NCIA), and simultaneously, maximises potential Malaysia-Thailand cross-border trade.
He said the government is currently finalising a study on the BEZ development involving four states - Perlis, Kedah, Perak and Kelantan.
“This study aims to assess and explore development proposals for the border area with a focus on key strategic border gates.

“Additionally, the Thai government is also finalising a similar study in collaboration with the World Bank to assess the potential development of their territory bordering Malaysia,” he said at the special chamber session at the Dewan Rakyat today.

He was responding to a question from Rushdan Rusmi (PN-Padang Besar) on whether the government intends to make the Padang Besar-Bukit Kayu Hitam Wang Kelian Corridor a model for the Malaysia-Thailand border economy.

Additionally, the proposed implementation of the Malaysia-Thailand BEZ development will be brought to bilateral negotiations through the Malaysia-Thailand Committee on Joint Development Strategy for the Border Areas (JDS) platform or other appropriate bilateral platforms.

At the same time, Mohd Shahar also welcomed Rushdan’s view that Malaysia should not simply be a transit route for trade between neighbouring countries, but rather play a more active role in dominating the market through value-added activities and downstream product processing.
Among the development initiatives being implemented in the area are the Perlis Inland Port (PIP), the Chuping Valley and the development of Bukit Kayu Hitam, he said.
He said PIP currently handles about 100,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU) per year, with the total handling expected to increase to 180,000 TEU per year.
“The development of border areas is among the government’s important agendas to strengthen the regional economy, increase cross-border connectivity and expand trade activities,” he said.

He said the implementation of strategies under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) 2026-2030 focuses on growth and high-value sectors including electrical and electronics, semiconductors, energy transition, digital technology, agro-food, halal products and tourism. — Bernama
a01e181a32a85a94: Once ‘famine food’, empty granaries have forced people along the Shire River to harvest water-lily roots in waters full of the reptiles The mid-morning heat in Malawi’s lower Shire River basin is already suffocating, but Beatrice Maseko cannot afford to look away from the water’s edge. Coated in grey, foul-smelling mud up to her thighs, the 34-year-old mother of four plunges both arms deep into the heavy sediment of a sprawling marsh. Her fingers feel blindly through the silt for the rough, bulbous roots of wild water lilies, known as nyika. Around her, a dozen other women move with deliberate, hushed slowness. No one splashes; no one speaks above a tense whisper. Just 50 yards away, where the marsh opens into the main artery of the Shire River, the silhouette of a Nile crocodile glides silently beneath the surface. Continue reading...
740043a912e4b600: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Malaysia and China are committed to expanding bilateral cooperation across various fields to create more opportunities that will benefit both countries.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was reaffirmed during his meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila.

“In my meeting with Premier Li Qiang, I expressed my appreciation for the warm welcome and hospitality extended during my recent visit to Hangzhou and Shanghai, which reflected the close friendship between Malaysia and China.

“I also conveyed my appreciation for the progress made in bilateral cooperation across various fields, as well as our shared commitment to further expand areas of cooperation that would benefit both countries,” he said in a Facebook post.
Earlier, Anwar attended the 29th Asean-China Summit, where he delivered Malaysia’s national statement.
On September 22, Anwar made a three-day working visit to Hangzhou and Shanghai at the invitation of the Chinese government, his fourth visit to the country since becoming Prime Minister in 2022.

Anwar said he also looked forward to Malaysia’s participation in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) Summit in Shenzhen on Nov 18 and 19, including the APEC CEO Summit to be hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping.
He expressed hope that the meetings would open up new opportunities to further strengthen economic cooperation and ties between Malaysia and China. — Bernama
2b12e0e01ef46ecb: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov xx — My Chemical Romance (MCR), one of the most influential rock bands of the 21st century, are back on tour with Malaysia among their stops.
MCR are set to bring The Black Parade 2026 tour to the TM National Stadium in Bukit Jalil on November 19 and 20.

Their Southeast Asian tour was originally scheduled for April and May this year but was postponed, with the band citing logistical considerations and the need to ensure the smooth execution of the regional leg.
The shows will mark their first performances in Malaysia in nearly 19 years, with the band once again bringing songs from their third studio album, The Black Parade, to local audiences.
The album celebrates its 20th anniversary this year, and much has happened since the band’s Malaysian debut in 2007.
MCR recap
Formed in New Jersey, US, in 2001, MCR comprise frontman Gerard Way (vocals), Mikey Way (bass), Ray Toro (lead guitar) and Frank Iero (rhythm guitar).
The band emerged with a distinctive blend of punk energy and emotionally charged songwriting that resonated with audiences worldwide.
Their mainstream breakthrough came with their second studio album, Three Cheers for Sweet Revenge, which includes hits such as I’m Not Okay (I Promise), The Ghost of You and Helena.
However, it was their landmark third album, The Black Parade, released in 2006, that cemented their legacy.
The concept album merged glam-rock spectacle with emo intensity through tracks such as Welcome to the Black Parade, Famous Last Words and I Don’t Love You.

After releasing their fourth and most recent studio album, Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys, in 2010, the band went on hiatus in 2013 before reuniting in 2019, returning to live performances after a six-year break.
Long live ‘The Black Parade’
View this post on Instagram
Since their reunion, MCR have continued to attract large audiences, particularly with their Long Live: The Black Parade stadium tour, which began in 2025.

The tour’s 2025 North American leg grossed approximately US$88.6 million (RM362 million) across 11 reported performances, selling over 448,000 tickets, according to box-office figures compiled by Touring Data.
The band have since extended the tour into 2026, taking their The Black Parade production to audiences across South America, Mexico, Southeast Asia, Europe and the United States.
MCR have also taken their stadium performances a step further with an elaborate theatrical production built around an expanding fictional universe.

This includes transforming venues into the fictional world of DRAAG, an authoritarian state in which the band are presented as ‘The Black Parade’, while incorporating mythology surrounding MOAT, a reconditioning facility where the band’s characters were held captive.

The production was brought to life with the help of TAIT, a US-based live-event production and engineering company headquartered in Lititz, Pennsylvania, which designed and built various staging, scenic and automated elements for the tour.
The company has previously worked with artists such as BTS member J-Hope on his Hope On The Stage tour.
“For their monumental return to the stage, MCR transformed stadiums into the fictional country of DRAAG – a surreal domain inspired by an old Russian train station and Gerard Way’s offbeat vision.
“TAIT helped transform each venue into a retro-futurist landscape of punk pageantry and cinematic storytelling,” TAIT wrote on its website.

Among the elements TAIT designed and built were a deep red main stage framed by distressed marble portals, a circular B-stage that brought the band closer to the audience, and a mechanical lift that raised the drum riser during performances.

The design also incorporated burning panels and pyrotechnic troughs to create a fire effect during Famous Last Words, alongside a manually operated firing-squad display that complemented the show’s dystopian themes.
Adding another layer to DRAAG’s fictional world is Keposhka, a writing system developed by Gerard Way and comic-book letterer and typographer Nate Piekos.

Inspired by Cyrillic lettering, historical propaganda posters and brutalist architecture, Piekos created 14 fonts for the project, which feature across the tour’s promotional materials, stage visuals and audience signs.
Beyond the stadium production, MCR have also expanded the album’s anniversary celebrations through Prelude to The End, an animated short film created with visual artist Lauren Tsai.

Drawing from Tsai’s own fictional universe and incorporating the album’s opening track, The End, the film offers another interpretation of the themes of creativity, identity and resistance that have long accompanied the band’s work.
Pop Shuvit to open
Malaysian rock band Pop Shuvit will once again share the stage with MCR when they open for the American rockers at the upcoming Kuala Lumpur shows.
The announcement marks a reunion of sorts, nearly 19 years after Pop Shuvit supported MCR during the latter’s first Malaysian concert at Stadium Merdeka in December 2007.
Beyond their shared stage history, MCR guitarist Ray Toro has also collaborated with several Malaysian musicians.
In 2023, Toro produced and featured on Pop Shuvit’s single Space Between Us, which also featured Butterfingers frontman Emmett on vocals.

Toro had previously contributed to Destination Nowhere in 2019 by Project E.A.R., a collaborative project featuring Malaysian musicians including Emmett and members of Pop Shuvit, alongside artists from other parts of Asia.

Public transport operator Rapid KL will extend operating hours across selected rail networks on November 19 and 20 to accommodate concertgoers, as it did during The Weeknd’s concerts earlier this month.
In a recent social media post, Rapid KL said the final boarding time at Bukit Jalil LRT station on the Sri Petaling Line is 12.30am for direct services towards both Putra Heights and Sentul Timur.
Passengers requiring transfers must leave the stadium earlier to catch connecting trains.
Those connecting to the LRT Ampang Line must board at Bukit Jalil by midnight to catch the final connecting service departing Chan Sow Lin at 12.13am.
The midnight cut-off also applies to those connecting to the MRT Putrajaya Line via Sungai Besi, where the last trains depart for Kwasa Damansara at 12.15am and Putrajaya Sentral at 12.34am.
Concertgoers relying on the LRT Kelana Jaya Line, KL Monorail or MRT Kajang Line must board at Bukit Jalil by 11.30pm.
Kelana Jaya Line passengers can transfer at Masjid Jamek to catch the final train to Putra Heights at 12.03am or Gombak at 12.17am.
For monorail users, the final connecting services from Hang Tuah depart for Titiwangsa at 12.08am and KL Sentral at 12.10am.
Those travelling on the MRT Kajang Line will need to make two transfers after boarding at Bukit Jalil by 11.30pm.

They must first switch to the Putrajaya Line at Sungai Besi by 11.45pm, then transfer again at Tun Razak Exchange (TRX), where the final trains depart for Kwasa Damansara at 12.10am and Kajang at 12.13am.
To ease traffic congestion around Bukit Jalil, Rapid KL urged concertgoers to use its Park and Ride facilities linked to the LRT Ampang, LRT Sri Petaling and MRT Putrajaya lines.

Motorists can access flat parking rates of between RM4.30 and RM5 per entry at official rail-operated parking facilities, provided they use the same Touch ‘n Go card to enter and exit the car park and pay their train fares.
Commuters can monitor real-time parking availability on concert days through the MyRapid Pulse mobile application.
The two Kuala Lumpur shows, organised by Hello Universe, initially sold 120,000 tickets within 90 minutes of going on sale in June.
The organiser subsequently released another batch of tickets on October 22.
Tickets for both days are still available via www.golive-asia.com.
b3eec9f862f1b67e: PETALING JAYA: Seorang lelaki yang sebelum ini disyaki menyamar sebagai juruiring Raja Muda Selangor dipenjara setahun dan dikenakan dua kali sebatan oleh Mahkamah Majistret Kuala Lumpur berkait dua tuduhan menipu dalam pembelian hartanah.
Majistret Amirul Asyraf Abdul Rasid memerintahkan tertuduh, Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, menjalani hukuman serentak bermula tarikh tangkap, iaitu 27 Okt, selepas dia mengaku bersalah.
Sementara itu, tunangnya, Nurul Nur Syahirah Kamarudin, 37, mengaku tidak bersalah selepas dua tuduhan dibacakan secara bersama, lapor Harian Metro.

Mengikut tuduhan, kedua-dua individu yang tidak bekerja itu didakwa secara bersama menipu dan memperdaya seorang selebriti lelaki berkaitan tawaran pembelian aset hartanah sehingga mendorong mangsa menyerahkan wang RM30,000 melalui dua pindahan kredit ke dalam akaun bank milik Al Zulfadly di Wangsa Maju pada 10 dan 12 Mei 2024.

Mereka didakwa melakukan kesalahan itu mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan, dibaca bersama Seksyen 34 kanun sama yang memperuntukkan hukuman penjara setahun hingga 10 tahun, sebat dan denda, jika sabit kesalahan.

Pendakwaan dikendalikan oleh Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Nurul Farhanah Arul Hisham, manakala Al Zulfadly diwakili peguam Mohd Ridzwan Warisi. Nurul Nur Syahirah pula diwakili peguam Shah Rizal Abdul Manan.
Terdahulu, Nurul Farhanah memohon mahkamah menjatuhkan hukuman setimpal kepada Al Zulfadly, sementara Nurul Nur Syahirah pula ditawarkan jaminan RM5,000 dengan seorang penjamin.

Mohd Ridzwan pula merayu anak guamnya hanya dikenakan penjara minimum kerana menanggung ibu, manakala Shah Rizal memohon jumlah jaminan minimum buat Nurul Nur Syahirah atas alasan anak guamnya tidak bekerja dan ditanggung ibu bapanya.
Mahkamah kemudiannya membenarkan wanita itu diikat jamin RM3,000 dengan seorang penjamin dan menetapkan 16 Dis ini untuk sebutan semula kes bagi serahan dokumen.
Dalam prosiding berasingan, kedua-dua individu tersebut didakwa secara bersama di Mahkamah Sesyen Kuala Lumpur atas empat tuduhan penipuan.

Mereka didakwa memperdayakan seorang doktor berkaitan urusan penjualan aset hartanah di Eco Ardence serta sebuah kenderaan mewah yang didakwa wujud, sekali gus mendorong mangsa memindahkan sejumlah RM155,000 ke akaun bank milik Al Zulfadly.
Al Zulfadly mengaku bersalah, manakala Nurul Nur Syahirah memohon dibicarakan, lapor Sinar Harian.
Hakim Mahkamah Sesyen Norma Ismail dijadual menjatuhkan hukuman ke atas Al Zulfadly esok.
Mahkamah turut membenarkan Nurul diikat jamin sebanyak RM15,000 dengan syarat tambahan melapor diri di balai polis secara bulanan serta menyerahkan pasportnya sehingga pelupusan kes.
Mahkamah Sesyen turut menetapkan 16 Dis bagi tarikh sebutan semula kes.
0d6b14da1cf57492: RANAU: A 15-year-old girl was seriously injured after being shot with a homemade firearm, known locally as a 'bakakuk', after being mistaken for a mouse deer while searching for frogs near a river in Kampung Tinanom here on Saturday night.
The incident occurred around 10pm, leaving the victim with about 13 injuries to several parts of her body, including her neck, chest, shoulders, hands and right knee.
Ranau police chief Superintendent Mursalin Mahmud said police had arrested a 40-year-old man, who is related to the victim, to assist in investigations.
He said the suspect, a farmer, was detained by a team from the Ranau district Criminal Investigation Division at 1.30pm yesterday.
"Preliminary investigations found that the suspect had gone hunting with a homemade firearm, moving along the Sungai Keliu area.
"When he was there, he spotted a light which he mistook for the eyes of a mouse deer and fired a shot.
"However, he later heard cries of pain before discovering that the person he had shot was the girl," he said when contacted today.
Mursalin said the victim had gone to the river with a family member and another man to catch fish and look for frogs before the incident.
The injured girl was taken back to the village before receiving emergency treatment at Paginatan Health Clinic.
"She was initially conscious but experienced breathing difficulties before being transferred to Ranau Hospital for further treatment.
"Examinations found that she had sustained multiple injuries believed to have been caused by the gunshot, including a fracture to her left wrist. She was also placed in an induced coma," he said.
The victim was transferred to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Kota Kinabalu yesterday afternoon for further examinations and surgery.
Mursalin said investigations also found that the suspect was believed to have discarded the firearm in the forest after the incident.

"The firearm has yet to be recovered, and efforts to locate it are ongoing with the assistance of the forensic team and the D10 division of the Sabah police contingent headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department.

"The case is being investigated under Sections 37 and 8(a) of the Arms Act 1960, while an application for a remand order has been made against the suspect to assist in further investigations," he said.
cf83f1c13b07e84a: PETALING JAYA: Seorang Adun pembangkang Kedah mempertikaikan kenapa derma melalui Yayasan Kedah Sejahtera yang berteraskan kebajikan rakyat, diguna membayar kos mahkamah kerajaan negeri.
Teh Swee Leong (PH-Kota Darul Aman), turut persoal tindakan sedemikian dibenarkan di bawah perlembagaan yayasan dan mendapat kelulusan sewajarnya.
“Saya tidak mempertikaikan keikhlasan penyumbang, tetapi ketelusan dan akauntabiliti dalam pengurusan dana awam mesti diutamakan.

“Mengapakah sebuah yayasan yang berteraskan kebajikan rakyat, digunakan untuk membayar kos mahkamah kerajaan negeri?” katanya menurut Bernama ketika sesi perbahasan Belanjawan Kedah 2027 pada sidang DUN Kedah, di Alor Setar.

Wakil rakyat DAP itu juga membangkitkan ke manakah lebihan kutipan daripada RM233,676.31 itu disalurkan, sedangkan hanya RM50,000 diperlukan bagi membayar kos mahkamah, susulan keputusan menolak permohonan kebenaran merayu berhubung isu pengharaman lesen premis perjudian, di negeri itu.
Beliau turut mempersoalkan adakah penyata penuh kutipan derma melalui yayasan itu, serta perbelanjaannya akan didedahkan kepada umum.
9913395fbec46c08: JOHOR BARU: Motorists travelling between Johor and Singapore have been warned to expect heavy traffic at the Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints during the year-end school holidays.
Singapore's Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) said congestion is expected from Nov 20 to Jan 3, 2027, with immigration clearance potentially taking up to three hours during peak periods.
The warning coincides with Malaysia's year-end school holidays, which run from Dec 5 to Dec 31 for Johor and other Group B states, including Selangor, Penang and Perak.
ICA said more than two million travellers crossed the land checkpoints during the Deepavali long weekend from Nov 6 to Nov 9, peaking at more than 553,000 crossings on Nov 6.
During that period, motorists departing Singapore at peak hours faced waits of up to three hours due to traffic tailbacks from Malaysia.
ICA also warned travellers against presenting incorrect passports or QR codes, noting such cases rose from 46 in July to 74 in September.
Those with incorrect documents or QR codes will be referred for further checks and barred from departing Singapore until valid documents are produced.
To speed up clearance, ICA urged travellers to use QR codes generated via the MyICA mobile application, which has boosted peak departure throughput by more than 35 per cent.
This improvement equals an additional 7,600 travellers per hour compared with pre-Covid-19 levels in 2019.
Motorists were reminded to maintain lane discipline, as queue-cutters will be ordered to make a U-turn and rejoin the queue from the back.
During the Deepavali enforcement operation, 11 departing motorists were caught committing traffic offences at Woodlands Checkpoint.
Six vehicles were ordered to make U-turns, while five drivers of foreign-registered vehicles were banned from entering Singapore for offences including crossing double white lines and queue-cutting.

ICA reminded travellers to ensure their passports have at least six months' validity, while foreign-registered vehicle owners must have valid Vehicle Entry Permits (VEPs), Autopass cards and insurance.
Since Nov 2, foreign-registered vehicles with unpaid traffic, parking or vehicular emissions fines cannot apply for or renew their VEPs and will be denied entry into Singapore.
Travellers were advised to avoid early morning and evening peak hours and check traffic conditions before setting off.
6778fafc07d2c202: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Laos have agreed to strengthen bilateral economic and trade cooperation, particularly in renewable energy, infrastructure, transportation and logistics, as the two countries mark 60 years of diplomatic relations.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the matter was discussed during his meeting with his Laotian counterpart, Saleumxay Kommasith, on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila, the Philippines.

In a Facebook post today, Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the meeting also served as a platform to strengthen bilateral ties, while allowing him to congratulate Saleumxay on his appointment as Laos' Prime Minister last month.
On bilateral trade, Anwar said total trade between Malaysia and Laos rose 28.7 per cent to US$55.9 million (RM228.5 million) in the January-August period last year.

He said both countries also agreed to intensify cooperation through the 4th Joint Commission for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC) Meeting, scheduled to be held in Vientiane in 2027, while finalising partnerships in higher education and tourism.
The 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits are being held from Nov 15 to 17 under the Philippines' chairmanship.
2635c47529736900: COTABATO CITY (Philippines): Philippine anti-narcotics agents, backed by police and Philippine marines, foiled an attempt by a Malaysian and his Filipino partner to sell 13.4 million pesos (RM858,000) worth of methamphetamines during a buy-bust operation in Tawi-Tawi over the weekend, an official said today.

The Philippine News Agency (PNA) reported that the suspects were killed after they opened fire on law enforcers during a buy-bust operation at around 4.50pm yesterday in Barangay Tubig Mampallam, Bongao, Tawi-Tawi, after sensing they were dealing with anti-narcotics agents.

Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) Tawi-Tawi provincial officer Abraham Solon Kalim identified the dead as Janimal Hajad, alias “Ungod,” a Malaysian national, and Sansibar Amirul Amil, a Filipino.

“Two unidentified women were also wounded by stray bullets and rushed to a hospital for treatment,” he said in his report to the PDEA-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao regional office here.
Kalim said government forces, backed by Philippine marines and police, seized about 2kg of suspected methamphetamines packed in two Chinese tea bags.
Authorities also recovered a pistol and a motorised wooden boat that the suspects allegedly intended to use to escape.
According to the PDEA, the gunfight erupted after the suspects noticed the presence of law enforcement operatives and attempted to flee aboard the boat while firing towards PDEA operatives.
Nobody was hurt on the government's side.
195129d3d5fdce3f: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia snapped a five-day losing streak, ending higher on Monday, supported by bargain-hunting in selected blue-chip counters, said an analyst.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 5.44 points or 0.34% to 1,588.03 from Friday’s close of 1,582.59.
The benchmark index opened 6.69 points lower at 1,575.90 and moved between 1,572.55 and 1,593.02 during the trading session.
However, market breadth remained negative with losers thumping gainers 673 to 375, while 522 counters were unchanged, 1,214 untraded and 16 suspended.
Turnover declined to 2.76 billion units valued at RM2.33 billion from Friday’s 2.84 billion units valued at RM2.36 billion.

Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the FBM KLCI's position near oversold territory, coupled with increasingly attractive valuations, could encourage further bargain-hunting, particularly in fundamentally sound blue-chip stocks offering sustainable dividends.
“Investors will also monitor Malaysia's upcoming economic releases, the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes and Nvidia Corp's earnings for fresh direction.

“While external uncertainties could prolong market volatility, we anticipate the FBM KLCI to consolidate within 1,580-1,600 this week, with selective accumulation likely to provide support at lower levels,” he told Bernama.
Meanwhile, Berjaya Research Sdn Bhd head of research Kenneth Leong said the local bourse has formed a bullish candlestick pattern, positioning it for a potential technical rebound.
“The immediate resistance levels are pegged at 1,600 to 1,616 points, while support levels are seen at 1,576 and 1,560 points,” he said.

Among heavyweight stocks, Maybank rose four sen to RM9.98, while Public Bank added one sen to RM4.55. CIMB climbed eight sen to RM7.16, while IHH Healthcare gained three sen to RM7.96. However, Tenaga Nasional decreased two sen to RM12.74.

In active trade, GIIB Holdings added five sen to 18 sen, while Ni Hsin was up 2.5 sen at 12.5 sen and Sime Darby gained eight sen to RM2.56. However, MMAG lost 0.5 sen to 2.5 sen and Zetrix AI was unchanged at six sen.

Among the top gainers, Nestle surged RM1.42 to RM94.42, while Malaysian Pacific Industries added 40 sen to RM37.60. Mega Fortris improved 37 sen to RM1.61, while Fraser & Neave went up 32 sen to RM20.10. Kuala Lumpur Kepong widened 24 sen to RM21.10.

UMS Integration led the decliners, falling 85 sen to RM6.15. MN Holdings dipped 21 sen to RM3.36. New Hoong Fatt Holdings erased 19 sen to RM1.14. Allianz Malaysia and Solarvest Holdings slid 18 sen each to RM19.10 and 3.90.
On the broader market, the FBM Emas Index rose 24.66 points to 11,761.55, and the FBM Top 100 Index added 26.08 points to 11,597.73.
The FBM Emas Shariah Index gained 23.76 points to 11,703.44, the FBM ACE Index fell 58.29 points to 5,004.85 and the FBM Mid 70 Index lost 20.02 points to 16,763.31.

Sector-wise, the financial services index rose 27.36 points to 18,539.56, the plantation index gained 54.89 points to 8,850.96, the industrial products and services index edged down 0.14 of a point to 169.95, and the energy index eased 5.92 points to 777.15.
The Main Market volume narrowed to 1.30 billion units worth RM2.08 billion from 1.32 billion units worth RM2.06 billion on Friday.
Warrants turnover declined to 594.27 million units worth RM61.95 million from 744.65 million units worth RM83.84 million previously.
However, the ACE Market volume rose to 859.38 million units valued at RM192.09 million from 774.69 million units valued at RM217.13 million on Friday.

Meanwhile, consumer products and services counters accounted for 225.41 million shares traded on the Main Market, industrial products and services (272.28 million), construction (113.10 million), technology (235.89 million), financial services (77.84 million), property (79.78 million), plantation (32.24 million), real estate investment trusts (11.22 million), closed-end fund (84,400), energy (95.51 million), healthcare (70.25 million), telecommunications and media (20.69 million), transportation and logistics (41.39 million), utilities (32.62 million), and business trusts (800).
