4588a6cde12efeff: MANILA: UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres expressed support Monday for fresh diplomatic efforts to engage with Myanmar's post-coup government but said that "violence needs to stop".
Guterres made the remarks in Manila, where Asean leaders agreed Sunday to pursue a "calibrated engagement" with the war-torn country.
Myanmar has been excluded from high-level Asean meetings since a military junta seized power in a coup in 2021, but the regional bloc is seeking a path towards normalising diplomatic relations.
"We have never opposed the idea that it is always necessary to engage with whoever is involved in a conflict," Guterres told a press conference on the sidelines of the Asean summit.
While "engagement is not appeasement", Guterres said the "intolerable violations of human rights in Myanmar" must end.
"Violence needs to stop, humanitarian access needs to be granted, and all those arbitrarily detained must be immediately released," Guterres said.
"And these are the conditions that could allow for what everybody should want (to happen), which is that Myanmar will find a way to move... to a true democratic situation."

Thailand has been leading efforts to normalise relations with Myanmar since coup leader Min Aung Hlaing was installed as civilian president this year following elections dismissed by monitors as a charade.

Bangkok has called for a "calibrated engagement" in an effort to implement Asean's long-languishing five-point plan to end the war between the military and a coalition of pro-democracy rebels and ethnic minority armed groups.
Asean leaders adopted that language on Sunday in calling for the pursuit of "a calibrated engagement with Myanmar through a phased and progress-based approach", according to the joint statement.
Guterres's remarks came as the UN's International Court of Justice prepares to rule on whether Myanmar committed genocide against its marginalised Muslim Rohingya minority.
359af05038365bf1: "Give me the child until he is seven, and I will give you the man." This saying about the importance of influence in early education is variously attributed either to St Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Jesuits, or Aristotle, depending on whether you wanted to entrust your very young son to Catholic priests or ancient Greeks. Fortunately for both groups, perhaps, neither of them ever said that, even though both certainly believed it.

Another group that certainly believes it is the cadre of tech company policy makers, which goes a long way to explain the cultural and legislative backlash to what happens to young people online. The least pernicious and longest established example of the catch 'em young principle is the educational discount for hardware and software. Apple has been the highest profile company to do this, with hardware discounts and aggressively positioned complete service packages for educational institutions, often integrated with funding authorities.

If you grow up using a package or platform, it becomes your first tech language and you're likely to become a lifetime customer. Microsoft has also played this long game, seasoned where it can with curriculum integration. Its latest wheeze, described by the company as educational platform evolution is a response to institutions' changing needs, with clearer pathways to adopting and enabling new technologies. Yada, as we say, yada.

The evolved platform removes email and Teams from the free student tier, while imposing the requirement for Windows hardware to qualify, along with comprehensive restructuring of higher tiers and storage not necessarily to the advantage of the educators.

This is the same sort of evolution to evolving needs as the British Empire brought to natives of other lands. Hello, India. Greetings, Africa. Whassup, America! These warships packed with gun-toting Brits are here to evolve your changing needs in local resource management.

Microsoft has realized what Imperial Great Britain adopted as its primary principle. If you can get your future, ahem, customers over a barrel, then not only can you imprint your brand on their minds, you can take their money. You have to come up with some balderdash to cover it, whether it's about civilization and progress or enabling educators to… oh God, these poor fingers can't even type this stuff.

Missing completely is the idea that educators' evolving needs may not include spending even more money on basic necessary services when budgets are stretched tight. Moreover, while existing uses of the old tier can stay on it until the end of next year, new sign-ups have to be on the Enhanced Speedy plans.

Keen students of history, especially those in the former colonial lands of Eastern North America, may care to refresh their memories of events some 250 years ago. It is quite natural, when being bent over a barrel ceases to be an amusing pastime, to seek a less barrel-shaped position.

In this case, the pressure to find alternatives has many elements. As well as the cost, support for Macs and Chromebooks becomes problematic. Both platforms are heavily represented in education at various levels, with the Macbook Neo thundering onto the battlefield with colors flying. Add to that the pressure towards digital sovereignty in Microsoft's own colonial outposts, the accelerants for an Old World version of the Boston Tea Party are only building. We even have a Boston of our very own. It's very nice.

Microsoft isn't threatening anyone with guns and rapine, not yet anyway, and the whipping away of free student access to email and Teams only feels like extortion because of the misery it is causing across the sector. It is perfectly legal for Microsoft to cause as much suffering coated in balderdash as it likes. It is also perfectly legal to return the favor by actively seeking a sector-wide migration strategy. There are pioneers to learn from, especially huge multi-state, multi-supply chain organizations like Airbus and the various European governmental entities that are some way down that path already.

This growing pool of expertise may be the most important factor in being able to react to Microsoft's efforts to turn education into a science fair experiment in high velocity frog boiling — one where the frog most definitely feels the heat — that and the growing distaste for the antics of American big tech.

It's not just the forcing of unwanted technology that makes the barrel increasingly unbearable, nor using that as an excuse to charge more, it's what the companies are actually trying to do in Europe. Google Chromebooks are nice. Google wolves invading your villages because the company illegally erased their ecosystem are not nice. You thought those Wi-Fi snooping Maps cars were bad?

The Microsoft educational platform "evolution" is foolhardy, counterproductive, and hugely tone deaf. It will not make it new lifetime customers, it will increase the speed at which its already hostile constituency grows resentment and appetite for radical action. Colonies revolt when the time is right, and empires are lost when arrogance and under-estimation of the situation combine with mismanagement and strategic blindness.
The US midterms showed how that storm is blowing in. To choose this time to provoke an entire global sector is functional illiteracy writ large. Perhaps Microsoft should get an education. ®
781292bb3d6ed286: TEHRAN, Nov 16 — Iran will not let UN inspectors visit its damaged nuclear facilities until the Middle East war has ended and the United States meets its conditions, a senior Iranian official said.

The remarks came days after the International Atomic Energy Agency urged Tehran to take steps towards resuming inspections, which have been suspended since last year’s 12-day war with Israel, when the US also struck Iranian nuclear sites.

“We will not grant the IAEA access to the facilities until Iran’s conditions are met and the war has permanently ended,” Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said in a televised interview late Sunday.
Iranian nuclear facilities were hit again during the Middle East war which broke out on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
IAEA inspectors visited Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant in September but have not gained access to other bombed sites including Natanz, Fordow and Isfahan.
Gharibabadi said the agency’s request to inspect damaged facilities was “likely aimed at assessing the effectiveness of American weaponry”.

Efforts to end the Middle East war have made little headway. Tehran is demanding that Washington unfreeze Iranian assets and lift sanctions, among other conditions, in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the vital energy shipping route it has blockaded during the conflict.
Iranian officials have said talks on Iran’s nuclear programme would come at a later stage.
Earlier this month, the US military announced a US$20 million (RM81.8 million) reward for information on Iran’s nuclear programme, a move Tehran called “repugnant”. — AFP
b8382b22820480b7: PARIS: French actor Gérard Depardieu on Monday withdrew his appeal against a 2025 conviction for sexual assault, accepting his guilt and apologising to his victims.
In a statement, Depardieu said he had often used "vulgar, sexually suggestive humour" on set and now realised "there is a line between cheekiness and offence."

He said he offered "his deepest and most sincere apologies to all those who may have suffered as a result", adding that he had chosen to pull his appeal as he had "come to realise that I belonged to a world that no longer exists."

Depardieu – a towering figure in French cinema, who starred in more than 200 films over five decades, including Green Card, The Last Metro and Cyrano de Bergerac – was found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a film set in May 2025.
He received an 18-month suspended sentence, with the judge saying he appeared not to have grasped the "traumatic" impact of his behaviour.
Depardieu still faces the prospect of a trial for allegedly raping actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. He denies guilt.
92b20436e2358c01: PETALING JAYA: Police seized suspected untaxed liquor, food, health and cosmetic products, as well as vehicles worth RM16.88 million in Op Taring Alpha 2 and Op Taring Alpha 5 in Sabah last month.

Bukit Aman internal security and public order department director Yusri Hassan Basri said three foreign men, aged in their 30s and 40s, were arrested during six separate operations in Kota Kinabalu, Manggatal, Inanam, Putatan, Tamparuli and Penampang between Oct 22 and 27, Bernama reported.

“Some of the premises raided had been operating these businesses for between two and 16 years. Further investigations are under way to identify the supply chains involved,” he said at the general operations force headquarters in Papar today.

Yusri said seizures under Op Taring Alpha 2 amounted to RM16.20 million, comprising 433,296 cans of alcoholic beverages seized in Penampang, 1,485 bottles of liquor worth RM742,500 in Manggatal, and 22,320 cans and three lorries worth RM1.4 million in Tamparuli.

Under Op Taring Alpha 5, police seized goods worth RM675,112 in three operations, involving 577 chilled and frozen processed food products and 251 health and cosmetic products at Centre Point, which were believed to have originated from the Philippines.
Police also seized 526 packets of frozen food products, 313 health and cosmetic products, 2,007 processed food products and 14,000 packets of various processed food items in Putatan.

Overall, he said that Op Taring Alpha 2 in Sabah had recorded 30 cases and 62 arrests so far this year, with seizures exceeding RM63.53 million, while Op Taring Alpha 5 recorded eight cases and one arrest, involving seizures worth RM1.8 million.
The department's special investigation intelligence unit, meanwhile, recorded 298 cases involving 493 arrests and seizures worth RM352.54 million as at last month.
579a062f0c26d604: TELUK INTAN: A man who robbed a motorist of RM4,030 at knifepoint and later stole gold jewellery and cash from KK Mart employees in separate incidents has been sentenced to a total of 10 years in jail and four strokes of the rotan.
However, Azizul Azmil Abdul Aziz, 26, failed in his bid to have the five-year jail term for the first robbery run concurrently with the sentence imposed in the second case.
Sessions court judge Norhamizah Shaiffuddin ruled that the sentences must run consecutively as the offences were committed on different dates and involved different victims.

In the first incident, at 4.10am on Jan 29, Azizul and an accomplice, who is still at large, approached a motorist who had stopped at an emergency lay-by along the North-South Expressway at Km366 to rest.
The duo threatened the victim with a knife and demanded money, prompting him to hand over RM4,030 before they fled on a motorcycle.
In the second incident on July 1, Azizul and another accomplice, who is also still at large, robbed two employees at a KK Mart outlet in Slim River.
They took the employees' gold necklaces and earrings before threatening them with a knife and forcing them to open the cash register. They then fled with all the cash inside.
Azizul was sentenced to five years in jail and two strokes of the rotan for each robbery after pleading guilty to both charges under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code.
In his appeal, he sought to have the jail terms run concurrently, citing his early guilty pleas, cooperation with police, the fact that his accomplices remained at large and that nobody was injured.
The court was also told that he was unemployed, unmarried and financially supported by his 53-year-old mother, who works as a People's Volunteer Corps member.
However, Norhamizah said public interest must take precedence over the accused's personal interests, noting that armed robberies caused significant trauma to victims.
"Such gang robberies occur far too frequently and cause considerable trauma to victims, particularly when deadly weapons are used, further heightening their fear.
"The court also took into account that none of the victims had recovered their stolen cash or jewellery," she said.
d3d418d2e089b8d3: NOVEMBER 16 — The world is entering an era when the use of military force is increasingly treated as an instrument of first resort rather than the last. Yet the more wars proliferate, the more urgent it becomes to strengthen the international conventions that restrain them. The world does not need fewer Geneva Conventions. It needs more of them. Come hell or high water.

The four Geneva Conventions of 1949 emerged from the devastation of the Second World War. Their fundamental purpose was to establish that even warfare must have limits. Civilians must be protected. Prisoners of war must be treated humanely. The wounded and sick must receive medical care. Hospitals and humanitarian personnel must not become deliberate targets.

These are not optional expressions of goodwill. They are legal obligations rooted in international humanitarian law. Yet the conflicts of the twenty-first century have exposed how difficult it has become to enforce these obligations. From Ukraine to Gaza, from Sudan to the wider Middle East, civilian populations have endured enormous suffering. The destruction of essential infrastructure, displacement of communities and interruption of humanitarian assistance have raised profound questions about the effectiveness of existing international mechanisms.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Displaced Palestinian children search of items that could be used as fuel for cooking amid a pile of garbage next to destroyed buildings at the Bureij camp for refugees in the central Gaza Strip October 6, 2025. — AFP pic

The problem is not necessarily that international humanitarian law has become obsolete. Rather, the mechanisms for ensuring compliance have not kept pace with the changing nature of warfare. The original Geneva Conventions were designed primarily around the realities of conventional warfare. Their Additional Protocols subsequently expanded protections, including those relating to civilians in international and certain non-international armed conflicts.
But warfare has changed dramatically.

Autonomous weapons, artificial intelligence, cyberattacks, drones and attacks against critical infrastructure have created new dimensions of vulnerability. A cyberattack against an electricity grid can disable hospitals without a single bomb being dropped. An attack against desalination facilities can deprive millions of people of drinking water. The disruption of maritime transportation through strategic waterways such as the Strait of Hormuz or the Red Sea can threaten food and energy security far beyond the immediate battlefield.

These developments require more than rhetorical reaffirmations of existing conventions. They require serious international negotiations on additional rules, clearer interpretations of existing obligations, stronger verification arrangements and credible enforcement mechanisms.

Artificial intelligence makes this particularly urgent. If military systems become increasingly autonomous, the question of human responsibility cannot be left unresolved. No government should be able to evade accountability merely because a military decision was delegated to an algorithm. The principle of meaningful human control over decisions involving lethal force deserves sustained international attention.

The history of international relations demonstrates that major wars often emerge not merely from disputes over territory or power, but from the gradual collapse of restraints on state behaviour. The First World War demonstrated the consequences of alliance commitments, militarisation and diplomatic failures. The Second World War demonstrated the catastrophic consequences of aggressive expansionism, racial supremacy and the systematic destruction of civilian populations.

The United Nations and the Geneva Conventions were among the institutional responses to these experiences. They were designed to prevent the recurrence of such catastrophes. Yet international institutions cannot survive on historical prestige alone. They must be strengthened by contemporary political commitments. The United States, China, Russia, the European Union and other major powers have particular responsibilities because their military capabilities and geopolitical influence affect the international system.

However, the development of humanitarian rules cannot become the exclusive preserve of the strongest states. The world cannot afford another arrangement resembling Yalta, where powerful governments negotiate the fate of smaller countries without their meaningful participation. Any renewed Geneva process must be inclusive.

For Asean, the strengthening of international humanitarian law is not an abstract diplomatic exercise. South-east Asia has experienced colonialism, occupation, revolutionary warfare, interstate conflicts and prolonged internal instability. Its member states understand the consequences of allowing military confrontation to overwhelm political dialogue. Asean has also spent decades developing institutions intended to encourage consultation, confidence-building and peaceful dispute resolution. These include the Asean Regional Forum, the East Asia Summit and the Asean Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus. Such institutions cannot replace the Geneva Conventions. But they can help build the political conditions necessary for their implementation.

Asean should therefore consider advancing a regional initiative supporting the modernisation and stronger enforcement of international humanitarian law. This initiative should involve not only the major powers but also smaller and medium-sized powers whose populations are frequently exposed to the consequences of conflicts they did not initiate. Indeed, the Indo-Pacific cannot be governed exclusively through military alliances and strategic competition. It requires a stronger architecture of humanitarian restraint. This is where Asean Will must become more important than diplomatic habit. Asean must demonstrate the collective determination to defend principles that protect civilians regardless of which major power is involved.

The moral foundations of humanitarian protection are not confined to Western international law. Islamic traditions of warfare contain important principles concerning the protection of non-combatants, the humane treatment of captives and restrictions on unnecessary destruction. Confucian political thought emphasises humane governance, moral responsibility and the obligation of rulers to exercise power with restraint. Western philosophical traditions, from Aristotle to the development of just-war thinking, have similarly examined the relationship between force, justice and political responsibility.
These traditions are not identical. Nor should their historical differences be overlooked. Nevertheless, they provide important intellectual resources for building a wider international consensus.

The Geneva Conventions should therefore be understood not as the exclusive achievement of any single civilisation, but as part of humanity’s continuing effort to limit cruelty. An international humanitarian order becomes stronger when its legitimacy is recognised across civilisations.

Military deterrence remains a feature of international relations. States will continue to maintain armed forces and defend their sovereignty. But military capabilities alone cannot produce a durable international order. The accumulation of weapons does not automatically generate political trust. Nor can military superiority resolve every historical grievance, territorial dispute or ideological disagreement.

Diplomacy is indispensable precisely because states disagree. International conventions provide a framework through which adversaries can establish minimum standards of conduct even when they cannot reach agreement on larger political questions. This is the enduring importance of Geneva. It is possible for governments to remain strategic competitors while accepting common humanitarian obligations. Indeed, the greater their rivalry, the more necessary these obligations become.

A renewed international initiative should concentrate on five priorities. First, strengthening compliance with existing Geneva Conventions, including independent investigation of alleged violations. Second, clarifying humanitarian protections in cyberwarfare and military applications of artificial intelligence. Third, reinforcing protections for hospitals, schools, water systems, electricity networks and other infrastructure essential to civilian survival. Fourth, improving humanitarian access and accountability in conflicts involving both states and non-state armed groups. Fifth, ensuring that smaller and medium-sized powers, regional organisations and representatives of affected populations participate meaningfully in the development of future rules.

Not every challenge requires an entirely new treaty. Some can be addressed through stronger implementation of existing law, additional protocols, interpretive agreements and institutional reforms. What matters is that international humanitarian protection does not remain static while the technologies and consequences of warfare continue to evolve.

The central challenge of our time is not merely the distribution of power among the United States, China, Russia and other major actors. It is whether international society can preserve a minimum standard of humanity amid intensifying geopolitical competition.
Without such standards, every conflict risks becoming a contest in which civilian suffering is treated as an unavoidable instrument of strategic pressure. That would be a dangerous regression.

The Geneva Conventions were created because earlier generations witnessed what happened when warfare was allowed to escape moral and legal restraints. Their achievement must not be squandered. The world needs more Geneva diplomacy, stronger humanitarian conventions and greater willingness to hold all parties accountable under international law. Malaysia and Asean should contribute to this effort by bringing together the major powers, smaller states, international organisations and civilisational traditions in a sustained dialogue.

The objective is not to abolish geopolitical competition overnight. It is to ensure that competition never becomes an excuse for abandoning humanity. Come hell or high water, the world needs more Geneva Conventions, not fewer. For when international humanitarian law collapses, it is not merely diplomacy that fails. It is civilisation itself.

* Phar Kim Beng, PhD, is Professor of Asean Studies at the International Islamic University of Malaysia and Director of the Institute of International and Asean Studies (IINTAS). Shahiran Kamaruzaman is an independent researcher.

4a6baf0419be5ca4: PETALING JAYA: EPF recorded a total investment income of RM83.32 billion in the nine months to Sept 30, a 30% increase from RM63.99 billion in the corresponding period in 2025.
The retirement savings fund said today total investment income for the third quarter of 2026 rose 3% to RM25.82 billion from RM25.07 billion in the same quarter last year, Bernama reported.
Equities income increased 3% to RM17.41 billion in the third quarter from RM16.95 billion in the same quarter last year, accounting for 67% of total investment income for the quarter.
It said global equity markets remained resilient during the quarter, supported by healthy corporate earnings, continued investment in AI-related themes, and generally favourable economic conditions.
“This provided opportunities for its fund managers to actively manage portfolios and generate value, contributing to the higher equity income,” it said.
Fixed-income instruments contributed RM7.12 billion or 28% of total investment income in the third quarter.

“While higher yields across key markets created valuation pressures on bond portfolios during the quarter, fixed-income investments continued to deliver resilient income and stability to the overall portfolio,” it said.
EPF said real estate and infrastructure generated RM890 million in income in Q3 2026, while money market instruments generated RM400 million, in line with return expectations for these asset classes.
As of Sept 30, total investment assets stood at RM1.55 trillion, with 38% invested globally.
It said international investments generated RM13.68 billion, accounting for 53% of total investment income for the quarter.
Total investment income for Simpanan Konvensional and Simpanan Shariah stood at RM21.39 billion and RM4.43 billion, respectively.
EPF also said it registered close to 659,000 new members in the first nine months of 2026, bringing total membership to more than 18.6 million.
Total contributions increased 9.34% to RM30.44 billion in the third quarter from RM27.84 billion in the corresponding quarter last year.

88d9b5adbe3aa6ba: BERLIN, Nov 16 — Germany coach Jurgen Klopp yesterday called for an end to Gianni Infantino’s time as Fifa president, saying he “did not think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter.”
Speaking in Berlin ahead of Monday’s Nations League clash with the Netherlands, Klopp said the next candidate for football’s global governing body should have the game’s interests at heart.
“I’ve been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense,” Klopp said.
“I didn’t think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that.”
President of Fifa from 1998, Blatter resigned in disgrace in 2015 amid corruption allegations.
Charges were brought against Blatter who was eventually cleared in two trials, but was banned from football by Fifa’s ethics committee.
Klopp added: “Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.”
Swiss Infantino succeeded Blatter as Fifa president in 2016.

He has come under heavy criticism for a series of decisions and proposals, including his plan to sell off part of the commercial rights of the World Cup and creating and then awarding the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize to US President Donald Trump.
“There are people who truly care about the future of football — people who aren’t driven by financial interests,” said Klopp.
“If someone like that were to step up — if someone like that were to become president — I think that would be a significant improvement.
“There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it.”
The next election for Fifa president takes place in March 2027. Only former Swiss footballer Ramon Vega and Japan’s Kozo Tashima have announced their intention to run against Infantino. — AFP
3609c11921f2cfc1: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia national team interim coach Tan Cheng Hoe wants his squad to bounce back from Saturday's 2-0 defeat to China by closing out 2026 on a winning note against Yemen in Zhaoqing on Tuesday.

Cheng Hoe admitted spirits had initially dipped after the loss to world No. 96 China, but insisted his players have quickly regained focus ahead of their final Tier 1 international friendly of the year.
"After the defeat to China, of course the players' morale was a bit down, but in terms of training and recovery, we have had pretty good preparation," he said.

"We know time is short for training, and looking at the atmosphere in this evening's session, the players appear to be back to normal. Focus and preparation are looking good, and we hope to close 2026 with a good result in our final match against Yemen."

World No. 133 Malaysia enter the clash as favourites on paper against 144th-ranked Yemen, though Cheng Hoe stressed the higher FIFA standing would serve as fuel rather than a burden for his depleted side, who are travelling without Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) stars and several injured Selangor regulars.
"Being in a better ranking position is not pressure for us. Instead, it gives us motivation and a challenge to maintain a result in our favour," he said.
"I think most of the players also want to make amends for the defeat to China, and this is the best opportunity to restore confidence in the team."
However, Harimau Malaya will be forced into at least one change up front after striker Fergus Tierney was sent off in the 90th minute against China for picking up two yellow cards.
Cheng Hoe said he is weighing three experienced attacking alternatives before finalising his starting XI.
"Tierney picked up a booking against China and will miss the match against Yemen, though we have two or three options to replace him, including Romel Morales, Paulo Josue and Syafiq Ahmad," he said.
"The coaching staff will pick the best option to fill in for Tierney."
At the back, Cheng Hoe is sweating on the fitness of defender Dominic Tan, who is racing against time to recover from a knock sustained against the hosts.
"After the match against China, we found that Dominic had a slight muscle injury problem. After two days, we see that he is still not at 100 per cent," he said.
"The medical team will determine whether Dominic can be fielded tomorrow, and we have other options ready if he is unable to play."

Despite the setbacks, the 58-year-old maintained that the two-match tour of China has served its primary purpose of blooding fringe players on the international stage ahead of next year's major campaigns.
"Our main objective in coming to Zhaoqing to face China and Yemen is preparation and exposure for other players to gain international experience," he said.
"To some extent, that experience will help us maintain our momentum and build towards the upcoming Asian Cup and World Cup qualifiers."
234a28a6d30f86b3: AMMAN: Jordan announced a ban on the Telegram messaging app on Monday, citing concerns that it was being used to spread extremism, weeks after a deadly attack on a church.
"We announce the blocking of the Telegram app in Jordan, in the framework of efforts aiming to bolster digital security and protext users," the Jordanian security directorate said.

It said the move came "in the context of the commitment to protecting society and countering any uses that could contribute to and facilitate committing cyber crimes, threats, blackmail or spreading illegal content."
It also said it sought to counter "attempt to spread radicalisation and extremism which affects national security."
The ban comes after the Oct 23 attack on a church in the southern Karak governorate that killed nine people and wounded dozens of others.
On Sunday, a court sentenced three men to death by hanging over the attack. Authorities described them as followers of a hardline Islamist ideology.
Jordan also banned TikTok in December 2022, citing the dissemination of videos authorities described as "inciting killing and chaos."
That ban followed protests over rising fuel costs, during which violence erupted, with one security officer killed.
3da65a0ef7b84caf: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) recorded a total investment income of RM83.32 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a 30 per cent increase from RM63.99 billion in the corresponding period in 2025.

In a statement today, the retirement savings fund said total investment income for the third quarter (3Q 2026) rose three per cent to RM25.82 billion from RM25.07 billion in the same quarter last year.
EPF chief executive officer Ahmad Zulqarnain Onn said the results for the first nine months reflect the resilience of its diversified portfolio and its front-loading strategy in previous quarters.

“We saw a deceleration of income growth in the third quarter, a trend which we expect to continue in the fourth quarter amidst weaknesses in global stock markets and rising yields in the bond markets.
“At the start of this quarter, risks around government borrowing, continued inflation and the valuation of artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks have become elevated,” he said.

Ahmad Zulqarnain said these developments require the fund to be disciplined in managing the portfolio, balancing opportunities against emerging risks while remaining focused on sustainable long-term returns and the retirement security of its members.

According to EPF, equities income increased three per cent to RM17.41 billion in 3Q 2026 from RM16.95 billion in the same quarter last year, accounting for 67 per cent of total investment income for the quarter.
It said global equity markets remained resilient during the quarter, supported by healthy corporate earnings, continued investment in AI-related themes and generally favourable economic conditions.
“This provided opportunities for its fund managers to actively manage the portfolio and generate value, contributing to the higher equity income,” it said.
As for fixed-income instruments, it said these contributed RM7.12 billion or 28 per cent of total investment income in 3Q 2026.

“While higher yields across key markets created valuation pressures on bond portfolios during the quarter, fixed-income investments continued to deliver resilient income and stability to the overall portfolio,” the fund said.

It said real estate and infrastructure recorded an income of RM890 million in 3Q 2026, while money market instruments generated RM400 million, in line with return expectations for these asset classes.
As at Sept 30, 2026, total investment assets stood at RM1.55 trillion, with 38 per cent invested globally.
EPF said international investments generated RM13.68 billion, accounting for 53 per cent of total investment income for the quarter.
Total investment income for Simpanan Konvensional and Simpanan Shariah stood at RM21.39 billion and RM4.43 billion, respectively.
On membership, EPF said it registered close to 659,000 new members in the first nine months of 2026, bringing total membership to more than 18.6 million.
It said active members rose to 11.2 million, with the ratio of active to inactive members improving to 60:40.
“Active employers increased to 646,686 as at September 2026, following 54,336 new employer registrations during the period,” it added.
Total contributions increased 9.34 per cent to RM30.44 billion in 3Q 2026 from RM27.84 billion in the corresponding quarter last year.

EPF said voluntary contributions rose to RM18.27 billion in the first nine months of this year, reflecting continued interest among members in building additional retirement savings beyond mandatory contributions.
“This growth was supported by EPF’s digital platforms, which made it easier for members to contribute voluntarily,” it said.
Meanwhile, it said, the number of Malaysian formal sector members contributing above statutory rates through i-Topup increased 6.9 per cent year-on-year to 244,350. — Bernama
c01946f6d8268945: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) is exploring the possibility of expanding the Kung Fu and Action Movie Special Screening into a larger annual event to promote martial arts and action films to new audiences.

The inaugural Malaysian edition offered free screenings of films from China, Hong Kong and Malaysia at GSC Mid Valley Megamall on November 14 and 15, bringing Chinese kung fu productions and local action films together in one programme.

Malaysian Film Festival director and Finas engineering director Raja Mohammad Adhzim Raja Ahmad said the initiative also aims to connect local and international filmmakers, allowing them to exchange ideas and explore ways to improve the quality of action filmmaking.

Organised by Finas, the Chinese Film Association of Malaysia (CFAM) and the Southern Film Culture Foundation, the event marked the Malaysian debut of the foundation’s travelling Kung Fu Film Festival.

The festival began in London in 2024 and has since travelled to cities including Toronto, New York and Copenhagen, with its Malaysian edition adopting the Kung Fu and Action Movie Special Screening name and incorporating local productions.

Adhzim said the decision to bring the programme to Malaysia this year followed growing interest in local action films observed during last year's 34th Malaysian Film Festival (FFM34), particularly following the success of Blood Brothers: Bara Naga, which won six awards, including the inaugural Best Stunt Direction award.
He added that the momentum has continued this year with the success of Tarung: Unforgiven, which is currently the highest-grossing Malaysian film of 2026.
“We need to build a stronger network and further improve the quality of our productions so that Malaysian action films can reach international audiences.
“Ultimately, our focus is to elevate the action film genre in Malaysia.”
Although the inaugural Malaysian edition was limited to two days, Adhzim said Finas would explore expanding the programme for future editions.
“For now, the focus is on having a two-day programme.
“We will see how things develop and explore the possibility of expanding it during FFM36 or FFM37,” he said.
“From what we can see, it is likely to continue as an annual event.”

Themed “Kung Fu Action Across Cultures”, the 2026 programme featured six Chinese films: Shaolin Temple (1982), The Way of the Dragon (1972), Ip Man 4: The Finale (2019), Blades of the Guardians (2026), The Shadow’s Edge (2025) and the animated film I Am What I Am 2 (2024).
The Malaysian line-up included Gayong 1 (2025), Mat Kilau (2022), The Assistant (2022), Kahar: Kapla High Council (2024), Tarung: Unforgiven (2026) and Takluk: Lahad Datu (2024).
The final screening on November 15 was The Way of the Dragon, the martial arts classic directed by and starring Bruce Lee, widely regarded as one of the genre's most iconic films.
Adhzim said future film selections would prioritise martial arts.
“The focus is on martial arts as a whole, although action films featuring fighting sequences will also be considered.
“The emphasis is on showcasing quality action filmmaking,” he concluded.
c78cdfe7b212dd37: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 16 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow today welcomed the implementation of seven projects worth RM84.26 million to address risks in coastal areas in the state.
He also welcomed the implementation of the Penang Integrated Shoreline Management Plan (ISMP) study, which began in June 2025 and is scheduled for completion in June 2027.

“The findings of the study will guide the state government and relevant agencies in planning development and managing coastal areas, taking into account current conditions and erosion risks,” he said in a statement issued today while referring to a reply to his question in the Dewan Rakyat recently.
He said the seven projects are to be implemented by the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra) through the Penang Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID).
According to the reply by Petra minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, the seven projects included three completed projects, two under implementation and two at the pre-implementation stage.

“They include the RM61.24 million project to construct outfalls and coastal erosion prevention structures in Batu Ferringhi and Tanjung Bungah, and the RM10 million project to construct and repair coastal bunds in Bagan Lebai Tahir,” he said.
The total expenditure on these projects as of September this year is estimated at RM16.8 million.
The minister said Petra is also conducting the ISMP study.
According to the ministry, 51 coastal areas in Penang covering 16.3 kilometres were identified as experiencing erosion.
“Of these, seven areas covering 5.6 kilometres were classified as Category One, with erosion rates of between 4.7 and 17 metres a year,” he said.

He said the DID does not have specific annual records of the number of critical coastal erosion incidents for the period from 2020 to 2026 and the available data is based on the National Coastal Erosion Study (NCES) 2015.
The NCES 2015 identified and assessed the extent of coastal erosion throughout the country.
The study classified coastal erosion into three categories based on the rate of shoreline retreat, the extent of erosion and its impact on the affected areas.
Category One is critical erosion, involving shoreline retreat of more than four metres a year, usually in areas with residents, economic activities, infrastructure and public facilities.

Category Two is significant erosion, with a retreat rate of more than one metre but less than four metres a year, while Category Three is erosion that is not yet serious, with a retreat rate of less than one metre a year.
df0bf4344783ca05: KUALA LUMPUR: The decision to reduce the land premium for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) from an initial estimate of RM4.67 million to RM1,000 has been described as unreasonable and potentially controversial.

National Council of Professors senior fellow Professor Emeritus Datuk Dr Teo Kok Seong said the vast difference between the two figures was difficult to justify, particularly as the decision was made shortly after a change in leadership overseeing the portfolio.
"The initial premium of millions of ringgit must have been based on concrete grounds and reasons," he said in a statement today.
Teo said the earlier premium estimate must have had a basis, despite KLSCAH being gazetted as a heritage site in 2007.
He said the proposal to reduce land premiums for several other heritage sites in Kuala Lumpur appeared to be an attempt to ease the backlash over the KLSCAH decision.

The decision to impose a nominal RM1,000 premium for the renewal of KLSCAH's land lease for 99 years was announced by Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh at the association's 103rd anniversary dinner on Nov 14.
Earlier, the Federal Territories Land Committee had approved the surrender and re-alienation of the land for institutional use on Sept 14.
Describing the reduction as insensitive, he warned that disputes over the decision could affect social harmony.

He also questioned the use of languages other than Bahasa Melayu at the announcement ceremony, saying the national language should have been given priority as the announcement involved an official government decision.
"The ceremony should have been conducted using the official language, but Bahasa Melayu was not given priority," said Teo.
He said the recurring issue, despite repeated reminders, should be addressed by government agencies.

Earlier, Yeoh said the reduction followed the conversion of KLSCAH's land status from commercial to institutional use, meaning it no longer carried commercial value and could not be developed for condominiums or shopping malls.
She said KLSCAH, which was gazetted as a heritage building in early 2007, had eight years remaining on its lease when it applied for the reduction.
The non-profit organisation had appealed based on its long history and heritage status, she added.
"On that basis, the valuation committee agreed to reduce the lease premium to RM1,000 since the land status has been restricted to institutional use only," she said.
5a10bc7e5e9eefea: AMMAN: The Telegram messaging application has been blocked across Jordan as part of efforts to strengthen digital security, protect users and prevent unlawful activities on online platforms, the Public Security Directorate (PSD) announced Monday.

Jordan news agency (Petra) reported PSD in a statement said the measure aims to curb the misuse of digital platforms for cybercrime, threats, extortion and the dissemination of illegal content, including extremist material that could threaten public safety and national security.
The directorate said the move is in line with existing legislation and reflects efforts to protect society from risks associated with the misuse of digital platforms.

It urged citizens to exercise caution when using social media and messaging applications, avoid interacting with suspicious accounts or links from unknown sources, and report illegal activities or content through official channels.

The PSD also emphasised the importance of parental supervision, calling on families to monitor their children's online activities, raise awareness of digital risks and encourage safe and responsible use of technology.
It advised parents to use available parental control tools to help protect children from harmful online content and interactions.
The directorate reaffirmed its commitment to taking necessary measures against cybercrime and other violations committed through digital platforms to safeguard public security.
3bd8dfb4dafe3327: PETALING JAYA: A man accused of posing as an aide to the Raja Muda of Selangor was sentenced to a year in jail after being convicted of fraud related to the illegal purchase of property.
Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, was also ordered to be given two strokes of the rotan.
Kuala Lumpur magistrate Amirul Asyraf Abdul Rasid handed down the sentence after Al Zulfadly pleaded guilty to two counts of fraud, Harian Metro reported.
He ordered the accused to serve the sentence from the date of his arrest on Oct 27.

Al Zulfadly and his fiancee, Nurul Nur Syahirah Kamaruddin, 37, were charged with defrauding and deceiving a male celebrity in connection with an offer to buy property assets, prompting two credit transfers of RM30,000 from the victim to Al Zulfadly’s bank account.
Nurul claimed trial and was granted bail of RM3,000 with one surety.
The prosecution was handled by deputy public prosecutor Nurul Farhanah Arul Hisham.
Al Zulfadly was represented by lawyer Ridzuan Marisi, while Nurul was represented by lawyer Shah Rizal Abdul Manan.
Separately, the pair were jointly charged in the Kuala Lumpur sessions court with four counts of fraud.

They were accused of deceiving a doctor in connection with the purported sale of a property asset at Eco Ardence and a luxury vehicle, which led to the doctor transferring a total of RM155,000 to Al Zulfadly’s bank account.
Al Zulfadly pleaded guilty, but Nurul claimed trial, Sinar Harian reported.
Sessions court judge Norma Ismail will sentence Al Zulfadly tomorrow.
She also set bail at RM15,000 for Nurul and ordered her to report to a police station every month and hand over her passport until the disposal of her case.
Both the magistrates' and sessions courts set Dec 16 for mention of her case.
5a90d88027969211: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's resilient economic outlook is expected to continue supporting its real estate market as it heads into 2027, according to international real estate technology group Juwai IQI.

Its co-founder and group chief executive officer, Kashif Ansari, said Malaysia was the only one among nine Asian economies to record a decline in food inflation from an already low level, while also benefiting from low headline inflation, steady economic growth and rising per capita income.
He said the country's resilient real estate market is due to several factors, including government policies, natural resources and an innovative population.
"When you look at the economic data, the clearest sign is this. Malaysia moved up two spots among the nine (economies), measured by gross domestic product (GDP) in US dollars.

"In 2025, Malaysia was the sixth-largest economy of the nine, but this year it looks like it has jumped to fourth-largest, passing two regional peers on the way, even though it has the second-smallest population of the nine, after Sri Lanka, with 34.2 million people," he said in a statement today.
Kashif said Malaysia's resilient economy had helped keep the housing market on firm ground, with 187,320 property transactions worth RM105.12 billion recorded in the first half of 2026.

He said Johor recorded the highest house price growth among the major states at 3.6 per cent, followed by Kuala Lumpur at 2.7 per cent, while high-rise property prices rose 0.9 per cent, faster than a year earlier.
"The Malaysian House Price Index rose 0.9 per cent year on year in the second quarter, to 234.7 points, and the average house price nationwide is now RM506,317.
"Families who are saving to buy a home are happy when prices remain steady and within reach. With inflation under control, interest rates have also remained stable," he said.
49c5105a2d4acae9: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Malaysia’s broader data-centre industry is expected to be less exposed to proposed United States (US) restrictions on remote access to advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips.
Demand for conventional cloud, colocation and enterprise computing from non-restricted customers should remain comparatively resilient.

MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB) said the proposed restrictions should not be interpreted as a blanket prohibition on US AI chip deployment in Malaysia or evidence of a structural slowdown in global data-centre demand.
“Rather, the measures could increasingly differentiate operators based on customer profiles, regulatory compliance and end-use transparency.

“Nevertheless, prolonged licensing uncertainties could delay certain AI-specific investments and, by extension, incremental demand for electricity, substations, grid connections and related engineering works,” it said in a research note today.

The investment bank said the proposed US restrictions were aimed at limiting China’s access to advanced AI capabilities, while under existing US export controls, the most advanced American AI chips generally cannot be exported directly to China without the required authorisation.

However, Chinese technology companies could potentially obtain equivalent computing capabilities by renting access to Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) clusters located outside China without physically importing the underlying hardware.
MBSB IB said operators with significant exposure to Chinese customers and those directly providing GPU-as-a-Service would be vulnerable to the new regulations.
“In a more restrictive or worst-case scenario, this could lead to delays or cancellations of planned AI DC investments.

“We caution against extrapolating these risks to Malaysia’s entire data-centre industry, as conventional cloud, colocation and enterprise computing demand from non-restricted customers should remain comparatively less exposed,” it said.

On YTL Power International Bhd’s alleged links to the NVIDIA-Megaspeed controversy, MBSB IB said it was important to distinguish the allegations surrounding NVIDIA and Megaspeed International from YTL Power’s own operations.

It said YTL Power had been caught up in the broad-based sell-off amid the developments, following allegations by Culper Research that Megaspeed was a major customer of YTL Power, with Chinese technology giant Alibaba being the undisclosed ultimate customer.

MBSB IB noted that YTL Power’s operations mainly followed a colocation model, whereby it provided space, power and cooling to third-party tenants rather than directly operating GPU computing infrastructure.
“Thus far, we have not identified credible evidence implicating YTL Power in the alleged chip diversion,” it added. — Bernama
8adc66e30e56fdf1: PETALING JAYA: The government has allocated RM10.62mil to upgrade infrastructure and facilities at the Long Lellang STOLport in Sarawak to improve operational safety after the fatal helicopter crash in September.
Bernama reported deputy transport minister Hasbi Habibollah as saying that resurfacing the runway would cost RM7.191 million, while RM1.2 million would be spent on the aircraft parking apron.
He told the Dewan Rakyat during a question-and-answer session today that resurfacing works are expected to begin in 2027, to be completed in the first quarter of 2028.

Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar) had asked what steps the ministry was taking to improve safety management and emergency response at all STOLports in Sarawak following the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash on Sept 8, which killed five people, including four health ministry medical personnel.
Hasbi said the Long Lellang STOLport would also receive a rapid intervention vehicle worth RM1.2 million to improve its emergency response capability.
He said the vehicle’s size and capabilities suited the rescue and firefighting needs of a small airport and that one unit was sufficient to meet the standards set out in Civil Aviation Directive 14.

Hasbi said Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd plans to recruit 15 personnel in stages to strengthen the STOLport’s operations and safety, starting with an airport manager, two technicians and one worker in June 2027.

He said the company plans to recruit seven airport fire and rescue personnel and four aviation security personnel in December 2027, noting that one aviation security officer and five members of the People’s Volunteer Corps currently handled security and emergency duties.

Replying to Shaharizukirnain Abd Kadir (PN-Setiu), who asked what action the transport ministry had taken after the Long Lellang crash, Hasbi said FDS helicopter operations had not been suspended because the aircraft had undergone airworthiness testing by the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia.
Hasbi said the helicopter involved held valid certificates of registration and airworthiness and had been confirmed airworthy at take-off.

“The investigation is continuing, and a final report on the accident must be prepared within a year. All the equipment involved, including the engine, have already been sent overseas for laboratory examination,” he said.
cebb78894b56d6e9: PETALING JAYA, Nov 16 — Three men charged with attacking a patron at a bak kut teh restaurant in Kepong will proceed to trial after the Sessions Court today rejected their bid for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA).

According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT), the application was filed by Wong Weng Luen, Lai Kae Bin and Wan Ken Fei, whose lawyers argued that the prosecution had yet to provide the documents required for trial preparation.

Judge Noor Aini Yusof subsequently directed the prosecution to furnish the outstanding documents to the defence before Jan 5, 2027, describing it as a final opportunity to do so. The judge said trial dates would be set next year.
The prosecution opposed the DNAA application, with deputy public prosecutor Adibah Iman Hassan informing the court that the investigating officer was still compiling the relevant documents.
Wong, Lai and Wan face a charge of causing hurt with a dangerous weapon to Andrew Teh Tiek Hua at a restaurant on Jalan Kepong, Metro Prima, at 2am on May 7.
The offence is framed under Section 326 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years upon conviction, as well as a fine and whipping.
Wong and Wan have remained in custody since they were charged in May after being denied bail. Lai is also being held on remand as he was unable to post the RM20,000 bail amount set by the court.
bcba2cd07f7dadd8: JERUSALEM: Two Israeli opposition leaders denounced Monday an "attempted coup" following press reports that outgoing prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month's election.

"As more and more details come to light, it becomes clear: this wasn't an attempt to disrupt the elections. It was an attempted coup," wrote Yair Lapid on X, who headed the opposition in the previous legislature and co-chairs the Beyachad list.
Israel's Channel 12 reported Sunday that on the eve of the Oct 27 election, Netanyahu's chief of staff Ido Norden had phoned in a complaint to the police about members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party.
Norden reportedly pointed the police to a purported intelligence source – a former employee of Netanyahu's office – who provided information that led to the arrest of three Raam members.
The three men were later released when the police determined that the information was unfounded.
Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats. His Likud party issued a statement denying the latest allegations.

The Israeli newspaper Haaretz also reported that David Zini, head of the Shin Bet domestic security service, sought to wiretap leaders of the other Arab slate, the Joint List, but the attorney general turned down his request due to lack of evidence.
Following the report, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen also denounced an "attempted coup by Netanyahu".

"If the findings are confirmed, this is a criminal mechanism that operated from the heart of government to rig the election results. Everyone found responsible must be held accountable, including Netanyahu," he wrote on X.
Raam's number two, former police chief Yoav Segalovitz, called for an urgent investigation.
"These suspicions require an immediate, independent and thorough criminal investigation that reaches everyone involved, at every level and in every role," he wrote on X.
"Netanyahu cried out that his election was being stolen, while he himself tried to steal the country and is still trying to do so now," he added.
Netanyahu's main rival, former army chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, wrote on Sunday that the caretaker prime minister "cannot remain at the head of the government for a minute longer".
Neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Eisenkot's opposition secured the 61 seats required to form a government following last month's election.
The two Arab parties, the Joint List and Raam, have indicated support for Eisenkot.
6cd3d24aa52811d5: KUALA LUMPUR: Dua bekas eksekutif kanan syarikat pembinaan mengaku tidak bersalah di Mahkamah Sesyen hari ini, atas tiga tuduhan pindaan melakukan pecah amanah dan bersubahat wang hasil kutipan penalti berjumlah RM72,000, membabitkan projek cadangan pembangunan kompleks pejabat di Putrajaya.

Bekas pengurus keselamatan dan kesihatan THP Bina Sdn Bhd Nasahruddin Ahmad, 56, dan bekas timbalan pengurus besar TH Properties Sdn Bhd yang juga bekas timbalan pengurus besar THP Bina Sdn Bhd Tengku Kamarolhisham Tengku Kamaruddin, 55, membuat pengakuan itu selepas ketiga-tiga tuduhan dibacakan di hadapan Hakim Rosli Ahmad.
THP Bina Sdn Bhd ialah anak syarikat milik penuh TH Properties Sdn Bhd (anak syarikat Lembaga Tabung Haji), yang menumpukan kepada bidang pembinaan dan pengurusan projek.
Terdahulu, Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Irna Julieza Maaras memberitahu mahkamah, terdapat pindaan pada ketiga-tiga tuduhan yang dihadapi dua lelaki itu.
Pindaan itu membabitkan ayat 'dengan tidak menyerahkan wang tersebut kepada THP Bina Sdn Bhd' yang sebelum ini 'dengan memasukkan wang tersebut ke dalam akaun Nasahruddin', dalam ketiga-tiga tuduhan.

Berdasarkan tuduhan pindaan, Nasahruddin yang diamanahkan wang hasil kutipan penalti ke atas kontraktor, iaitu syarikat Fourth Wave Sdn Bhd berjumlah RM72,000, didakwa melakukan pecah amanah dengan tidak menyerahkan wang berkenaan kepada THP Bina Sdn Bhd.

Wang hasil kutipan penalti itu membabitkan projek cadangan pembangunan kompleks pejabat di Presint 3, Putrajaya, melibatkan beberapa tingkat pejabat di Blok A, B, C dan D, sebuah auditorium dan tempat letak kereta bawah tanah untuk Tetuan THP Bina Sdn Bhd.

Dia didakwa melakukan kesalahan itu di Kompleks Islam Putrajaya di Presint 3 antara 26 April 2013 hingga 12 Ogos 2015, yang mengikut Seksyen 409 Kanun Keseksaan memperuntukkan hukuman penjara maksimum 20 tahun serta sebatan dan boleh didenda, jika sabit kesalahan.

Sementara itu, Tengku Kamarolhisham berhadapan tiga tuduhan pindaaan bersubahat, dengan mengarahkan Nasahruddin untuk tidak menyerahkan wang berkenaan kepada THP Bina Sdn Bhd pada tempat dan masa sama, mengikut Seksyen 109 Kanun Keseksaan, dibaca bersama-sama Seksyen 409 kanun sama.
Pada prosiding hari ini, kedua-dua lelaki itu diwakili peguam Fahmi Abd Moin dan mahkamah menetapkan sebutan kes pada 17 Dis untuk serahan dokumen.
175fae7faa791855: BEIJING, Nov 16 — China said today that President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin would discuss “world peace” when they hold their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen this week.

The three leaders will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations”, foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a news briefing, hours after Beijing confirmed the meeting.
“It will be of ground-breaking significance,” she said.
The trilateral is expected to happen on Thursday on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leaders in the southern Chinese city.
The Kremlin and the White House both previously confirmed the three-way meeting.
Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said.
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said Xi showed “irritation” in a recent meeting when the idea of the trilateral talks covering Ukraine came up.
“He explicitly pointed out that this is a European conflict, in which the Europeans must also be at the table,” Steinmeier told ARD.
On nuclear disarmament, China has long insisted that the United States and Russia reduce their own giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its own stockpile. — AFP
